/></a></div></div></div><div class="trow" style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Ince_Minaret_Medrese" title="Ince Minaret Medrese">Ince Minaret Medrese</a> in <a href="/wiki/Konya" title="Konya">Konya</a> (left), <a href="/wiki/%C3%87ifte_Minareli_Medrese_(Erzurum)" title="Çifte Minareli Medrese (Erzurum)">Çifte Minareli Medrese</a> in <a href="/wiki/Erzurum" title="Erzurum">Erzurum</a> (centre) and <a href="/wiki/Divri%C4%9Fi_Great_Mosque_and_Hospital" title="Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital">Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital</a> (right) are among the finest examples of <a href="/wiki/Seljuk_architecture" title="Seljuk architecture">Seljuk architecture</a>.</div></div></div></div>
<p>In 1243, the Seljuk armies were defeated by the <a href="/wiki/Mongol_Empire" title="Mongol Empire">Mongols</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_K%C3%B6se_Da%C4%9F" title="Battle of Köse Dağ">Battle of Köse Dağ</a>, causing the Seljuk Empire's power to slowly disintegrate. In its wake, one of the <a href="/wiki/Anatolian_beyliks" title="Anatolian beyliks">Turkish principalities</a> governed by <a href="/wiki/Osman_I" title="Osman I">Osman I</a> would evolve over the next 200 years into the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>. The Ottomans completed their conquest of the Byzantine Empire by <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople" title="Fall of Constantinople">capturing its capital, Constantinople</a>, in 1453: their commander thenceforth being known as <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_the_Conqueror" class="mw-redirect" title="Mehmed the Conqueror">Mehmed the Conqueror</a>.
</p><p>Following the end of the <a href="/wiki/Reconquista" title="Reconquista">Reconquista</a> and the subsequent <a href="/wiki/Alhambra_Decree" title="Alhambra Decree">Alhambra Decree</a> of 31 March 1492, which resulted in the expulsion of non-Christians (Muslims and Jews) from <a href="/wiki/Iberia" class="mw-redirect" title="Iberia">Iberia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Naples" title="Kingdom of Naples">southern Italy</a> controlled by the Crowns of <a href="/wiki/Crown_of_Castile" title="Crown of Castile">Castile</a> and <a href="/wiki/Crown_of_Aragon" title="Crown of Aragon">Aragon</a> (and later by the <a href="/wiki/Spanish_Empire" title="Spanish Empire">Spanish Empire</a>), a large number of <a href="/wiki/Al-Andalus" title="Al-Andalus">Andalusian Muslims</a> and <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_the_Ottoman_Empire#Influx_of_Sephardic_Jews_from_Iberia" title="History of the Jews in the Ottoman Empire">Sephardic Jews</a> <a href="/wiki/Bayezid_II#Jewish_and_Muslim_immigration" title="Bayezid II">emigrated</a> to the Ottoman Empire during the reigns of Sultan <a href="/wiki/Bayezid_II" title="Bayezid II">Bayezid II</a> and his successors, settling primarily in <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a>, <a href="/wiki/Izmir" class="mw-redirect" title="Izmir">Izmir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thessaloniki" title="Thessaloniki">Selanik</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bursa" title="Bursa">Bursa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Edirne" title="Edirne">Edirne</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-JE_460_109-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-JE_460-109">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tleft"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:234px;max-width:234px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:232px;max-width:232px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg/230px-Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg" decoding="async" width="230" height="115" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg/345px-Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg/460px-Topkap%C4%B1_-_01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3635" data-file-height="1817" /></a></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:232px;max-width:232px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace,_Istanbul_cropped.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg/230px-Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg" decoding="async" width="230" height="121" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg/345px-Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg/460px-Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace%2C_Istanbul_cropped.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4740" data-file-height="2484" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Topkap%C4%B1_Palace" title="Topkapı Palace">Topkapı</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace" title="Dolmabahçe Palace">Dolmabahçe</a> palaces in <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a> were the primary residences of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman</a> <a href="/wiki/List_of_sultans_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="List of sultans of the Ottoman Empire">Sultans</a> in 1465–1856<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes_110-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes-110">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup> and 1856–1922,<sup id="cite_ref-dolmabahcepalace_111-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dolmabahcepalace-111">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> respectively.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>In 1514, Sultan <a href="/wiki/Selim_I" title="Selim I">Selim I</a> (1512–1520) successfully expanded the empire's southern and eastern borders by defeating Shah <a href="/wiki/Ismail_I" title="Ismail I">Ismail I</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Safavid_dynasty" title="Safavid dynasty">Safavid dynasty</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Chaldiran" title="Battle of Chaldiran">Battle of Chaldiran</a>. In 1517, Selim I expanded Ottoman rule into <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Algeria" title="Ottoman Algeria">Algeria</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Mamluk_War_(1516%E2%80%931517)" title="Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)">Egypt</a>, and created a naval presence in the <a href="/wiki/Red_Sea" title="Red Sea">Red Sea</a>. Subsequently, a contest started between the Ottoman and <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_Empire" title="Portuguese Empire">Portuguese</a> empires to become the dominant sea power in the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_naval_expeditions_in_the_Indian_Ocean" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman naval expeditions in the Indian Ocean">a number of naval battles</a> in the Red Sea, the <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Sea" title="Arabian Sea">Arabian Sea</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Persian_Gulf" title="Persian Gulf">Persian Gulf</a>. The Portuguese presence in the Indian Ocean was perceived as a threat to the Ottoman monopoly over the <a href="/wiki/Silk_Road" title="Silk Road">ancient trade routes</a> between <a href="/wiki/East_Asia" title="East Asia">East Asia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Western_Europe" title="Western Europe">Western Europe</a>. Despite the increasingly prominent European presence, the Ottoman Empire's trade with the east continued to flourish until the second half of the 18th century.<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Ottoman Empire's power and prestige peaked in the 16th and 17th centuries, particularly during the reign of <a href="/wiki/Suleiman_the_Magnificent" title="Suleiman the Magnificent">Suleiman the Magnificent</a>, who personally instituted major legislative changes relating to society, education, taxation and criminal law.
</p><p>The empire was often at odds with the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire" title="Holy Roman Empire">Holy Roman Empire</a> in its steady advance towards <a href="/wiki/Central_Europe" title="Central Europe">Central Europe</a> through the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a> and the southern part of the <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-autogenerated1_113-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autogenerated1-113">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Navy" title="Ottoman Navy">Ottoman Navy</a> contended with several Holy Leagues, such as those in <a href="/wiki/Holy_League_(1538)" title="Holy League (1538)">1538</a>, <a href="/wiki/Holy_League_(1571)" title="Holy League (1571)">1571</a>, <a href="/wiki/Holy_League_(1684)" title="Holy League (1684)">1684</a> and <a href="/wiki/Holy_League_(1717)" title="Holy League (1717)">1717</a> (composed primarily of <a href="/wiki/Habsburg_Spain" title="Habsburg Spain">Habsburg Spain</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa" title="Republic of Genoa">Republic of Genoa</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Venice" title="Republic of Venice">Republic of Venice</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Knights_Hospitaller" title="Knights Hospitaller">Knights of St. John</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Papal_States" title="Papal States">Papal States</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Grand_Duchy_of_Tuscany" title="Grand Duchy of Tuscany">Grand Duchy of Tuscany</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Duchy_of_Savoy" title="Duchy of Savoy">Duchy of Savoy</a>), for the control of the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a>.
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:332px;"><a href="/wiki/File:OttomanEmpireIn1683.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/OttomanEmpireIn1683.png/330px-OttomanEmpireIn1683.png" decoding="async" width="330" height="311" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/OttomanEmpireIn1683.png/495px-OttomanEmpireIn1683.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/OttomanEmpireIn1683.png/660px-OttomanEmpireIn1683.png 2x" data-file-width="1966" data-file-height="1850" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:OttomanEmpireIn1683.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Vienna" title="Battle of Vienna">second Ottoman siege of Vienna</a> in 1683 (the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Vienna_(1529)" title="Siege of Vienna (1529)">first siege</a> was in 1529) initiated the <a href="/wiki/Great_Turkish_War" title="Great Turkish War">Great Turkish War</a> (1683–1699) between the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottomans</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Holy_League_(1684)" title="Holy League (1684)">Holy League</a>.</div></div></div>
<p>In the east, the Ottomans were often at war with Safavid Persia over conflicts stemming from territorial disputes or religious differences between the 16th and 18th centuries.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Ottoman-Persian_Wars" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman-Persian Wars">Ottoman wars with Persia</a> continued as the <a href="/wiki/Zand_dynasty" title="Zand dynasty">Zand</a>, <a href="/wiki/Afsharid_dynasty" title="Afsharid dynasty">Afsharid</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Qajar_dynasty" title="Qajar dynasty">Qajar</a> dynasties succeeded the Safavids in Iran, until the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Persian_War_(1821%E2%80%931823)" title="Ottoman–Persian War (1821–1823)">first half of the 19th century</a>.
</p><p>Even further east, there was an extension of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Habsburg_wars" title="Ottoman–Habsburg wars">Habsburg-Ottoman conflict</a>, in that the Ottomans also had to <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_expedition_to_Aceh" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman expedition to Aceh">send soldiers</a> to their farthest and easternmost vassal and territory, the <a href="/wiki/Aceh_Sultanate" title="Aceh Sultanate">Aceh Sultanate</a><sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> in <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>, to defend it from European colonizers as well as the <a href="/wiki/Juan_de_Salcedo" title="Juan de Salcedo">Latino invaders</a> who had crossed from <a href="/wiki/Latin_America" title="Latin America">Latin America</a> and had Christianized the formerly Muslim-dominated <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_the_Philippines" title="Islam in the Philippines">Philippines</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>From the 16th to the early 20th centuries, the Ottoman Empire also <a href="/wiki/Russo-Turkish_Wars" class="mw-redirect" title="Russo-Turkish Wars">fought twelve wars</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia" title="Tsardom of Russia">Russian Tsardom</a> and <a href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Empire</a>. These were initially about Ottoman territorial expansion and consolidation in southeastern and eastern Europe; but starting from the <a href="/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1768%E2%80%931774)" title="Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774)">Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774)</a>, they became more about the survival of the Ottoman Empire, which had begun to lose its strategic territories on the northern <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> coast to the advancing Russians.
</p><p>From the second half of the 18th century onwards, the <a href="/wiki/Decline_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Decline of the Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire began to decline</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Tanzimat" title="Tanzimat">Tanzimat</a> reforms, initiated by <a href="/wiki/Mahmud_II" title="Mahmud II">Mahmud II</a> just before his death in 1839, aimed to modernise the Ottoman state in line with the progress that had been made in Western Europe. The efforts of <a href="/wiki/Midhat_Pasha" title="Midhat Pasha">Midhat Pasha</a> during the late Tanzimat era led the Ottoman <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_constitution_of_1876" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman constitution of 1876">constitutional movement of 1876</a>, which introduced the <a href="/wiki/First_Constitutional_Era" title="First Constitutional Era">First Constitutional Era</a>, but these efforts proved to be inadequate in most fields, and failed to stop the <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Dissolution of the Ottoman Empire">dissolution of the empire</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OttoTurkVis_118-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OttoTurkVis-118">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:272px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg/270px-Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg" decoding="async" width="270" height="203" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg/405px-Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg/540px-Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4608" data-file-height="3456" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Suleymaniye_DSCF3573.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/S%C3%BCleymaniye_Mosque" title="Süleymaniye Mosque">Süleymaniye Mosque</a> is the largest Ottoman imperial mosque located on the <a href="/wiki/Seven_hills_of_Istanbul" title="Seven hills of Istanbul">Third Hill</a> of <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a>. The mosque was commissioned by <a href="/wiki/Suleiman_the_Magnificent" title="Suleiman the Magnificent">Suleiman the Magnificent</a> and designed by the imperial architect <a href="/wiki/Mimar_Sinan" title="Mimar Sinan">Mimar Sinan</a>.</div></div></div>
<p>As the empire gradually shrank in size, military power and wealth; especially after the <a href="/wiki/Great_Eastern_Crisis" title="Great Eastern Crisis">Ottoman economic crisis and default</a> in 1875<sup id="cite_ref-NiallFergusonFT_119-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NiallFergusonFT-119">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> which led to uprisings in the Balkan provinces that culminated in the <a href="/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1877%E2%80%931878)" title="Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)">Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)</a>; many Balkan Muslims migrated to the Empire's heartland in Anatolia,<sup id="cite_ref-Illinois2009_120-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Illinois2009-120">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup> along with the <a href="/wiki/Circassians" title="Circassians">Circassians</a> fleeing the <a href="/wiki/Russian%E2%80%93Circassian_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian–Circassian War">Russian conquest</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Russian_conquest_of_the_Caucasus" title="Russian conquest of the Caucasus">Caucasus</a>. According to some estimates, 800,000 Muslim <a href="/wiki/Circassians" title="Circassians">Circassians</a> died during the <a href="/wiki/Circassian_genocide" title="Circassian genocide">Circassian genocide</a> in the territory of present-day Russia, the survivors of which sought refuge in the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>, mostly settling in the provinces of present-day Turkey. The decline of the Ottoman Empire led to a <a href="/wiki/Rise_of_nationalism_under_the_Ottoman_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Rise of nationalism under the Ottoman Empire">rise in nationalist sentiment among its various subject peoples</a>, leading to increased ethnic tensions which occasionally burst into violence, such as the <a href="/wiki/Hamidian_massacres" title="Hamidian massacres">Hamidian massacres</a> of <a href="/wiki/Armenians_in_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Armenians in the Ottoman Empire">Armenians</a>, which claimed up to 300,000 lives.<sup id="cite_ref-nzhistory.net.nz_122-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nzhistory.net.nz-122">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The loss of <a href="/wiki/Rumelia" title="Rumelia">Rumelia</a> (Ottoman territories in Europe) with the <a href="/wiki/First_Balkan_War" title="First Balkan War">First Balkan War</a> (1912–1913) was followed by the arrival of millions of Muslim refugees (<i><a href="/wiki/Muhacir" title="Muhacir">muhacir</a></i>) to Istanbul and Anatolia.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup> Historically, the <a href="/wiki/Rumelia_Eyalet" title="Rumelia Eyalet">Rumelia Eyalet</a> and <a href="/wiki/Anatolia_Eyalet" title="Anatolia Eyalet">Anatolia Eyalet</a> had formed the <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Administrative divisions of the Ottoman Empire">administrative</a> core of the Ottoman Empire, with their governors titled <a href="/wiki/Beylerbey" title="Beylerbey">Beylerbeyi</a> participating in the Sultan's <a href="/wiki/Imperial_Council_(Ottoman_Empire)" title="Imperial Council (Ottoman Empire)">Divan</a>, so the loss of all Balkan provinces beyond the <a href="/wiki/K%C4%B1y%C4%B1k%C3%B6y" title="Kıyıköy">Midye</a>-<a href="/wiki/Enez" title="Enez">Enez</a> border line according to the <a href="/wiki/London_Conference_of_1912%E2%80%9313" class="mw-redirect" title="London Conference of 1912–13">London Conference of 1912–13</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_London_(1913)" title="Treaty of London (1913)">Treaty of London (1913)</a> was a major shock for the Ottoman society and led to the <a href="/wiki/1913_Ottoman_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1913 Ottoman coup d&#39;état">1913 Ottoman coup d'état</a>. In the <a href="/wiki/Second_Balkan_War" title="Second Balkan War">Second Balkan War</a> (1913) the Ottomans managed to recover their former capital <a href="/wiki/Edirne" title="Edirne">Edirne</a> (Adrianople) and its surrounding areas in <a href="/wiki/East_Thrace" title="East Thrace">East Thrace</a>, which was formalised with the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Constantinople_(1913)" title="Treaty of Constantinople (1913)">Treaty of Constantinople (1913)</a>. The 1913 coup d'état effectively put the country under the control of the <a href="/wiki/Three_Pashas" title="Three Pashas">Three Pashas</a>, making sultans <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_V" title="Mehmed V">Mehmed V</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_VI" title="Mehmed VI">Mehmed VI</a> largely symbolic figureheads with no real political power.
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:332px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg/330px-Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg" decoding="async" width="330" height="213" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg/495px-Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg/660px-Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1640" data-file-height="1060" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Central_Powers_monarchs_postcard.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1126788409"/><div class="plainlist nowrap"><ul><li>Monarchs of the <a href="/wiki/Central_Powers" title="Central Powers">Central Powers</a> on a <a href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">WWI</a> postcard:</li><li>Kaiser <a href="/wiki/Wilhelm_II,_German_Emperor" title="Wilhelm II, German Emperor">Wilhelm II</a> of Germany;</li><li>Kaiser and King <a href="/wiki/Franz_Joseph_I_of_Austria" title="Franz Joseph I of Austria">Franz Joseph</a> of Austria-Hungary;</li><li>Sultan <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_V" title="Mehmed V">Mehmed V</a> of the Ottoman Empire;</li><li>Tsar <a href="/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Bulgaria" title="Ferdinand I of Bulgaria">Ferdinand I</a> of Bulgaria</li></ul></div></div></div></div>
<p>The Ottoman Empire entered <a href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">World War I</a> on the side of the <a href="/wiki/Central_Powers" title="Central Powers">Central Powers</a> and was ultimately defeated. The Ottomans successfully defended the <a href="/wiki/Dardanelles" title="Dardanelles">Dardanelles</a> strait during the <a href="/wiki/Gallipoli_campaign" title="Gallipoli campaign">Gallipoli campaign</a> (1915–1916) and achieved initial victories against British forces in the first two years of the <a href="/wiki/Mesopotamian_campaign" title="Mesopotamian campaign">Mesopotamian campaign</a>, such as the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Kut" title="Siege of Kut">Siege of Kut</a> (1915–1916); but the <a href="/wiki/Arab_Revolt" title="Arab Revolt">Arab Revolt</a> (1916–1918) turned the tide against the Ottomans in the Middle East. In the <a href="/wiki/Caucasus_campaign" title="Caucasus campaign">Caucasus campaign</a>, however, the Russian forces had the upper hand from the beginning, especially after the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Sarikamish" title="Battle of Sarikamish">Battle of Sarikamish</a> (1914–1915). Russian forces advanced into northeastern Anatolia and controlled the major cities there until retreating from World War I with the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Brest-Litovsk" title="Treaty of Brest-Litovsk">Treaty of Brest-Litovsk</a> following the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Revolution" title="Russian Revolution">Russian Revolution</a> (1917). During the war, the empire's Armenian subjects were <a href="/wiki/Tehcir_Law" class="mw-redirect" title="Tehcir Law">deported</a> to <a href="/wiki/Syria" title="Syria">Syria</a> as part of the <a href="/wiki/Armenian_genocide" title="Armenian genocide">Armenian genocide</a>. As a result, an estimated 600,000<sup id="cite_ref-britannica-ag_124-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britannica-ag-124">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> to more than 1 million,<sup id="cite_ref-britannica-ag_124-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britannica-ag-124">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> or up to 1.5 million<sup id="cite_ref-umichigan_125-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-umichigan-125">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-jfreedman_126-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jfreedman-126">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-totten-et-al_127-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-totten-et-al-127">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Armenians_in_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Armenians in the Ottoman Empire">Armenians</a> were killed. The Turkish government has <a href="/wiki/Armenian_genocide_denial" title="Armenian genocide denial">refused to acknowledge</a><sup id="cite_ref-Tatz_24-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tatz-24">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> the events as <a href="/wiki/Genocide" title="Genocide">genocide</a> and states that Armenians were only <a href="/wiki/Population_transfer" title="Population transfer">"relocated</a>" from the eastern war zone.<sup id="cite_ref-129" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-129">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Late_Ottoman_genocides" title="Late Ottoman genocides">Genocidal campaigns</a> were also committed against the empire's other minority groups such as the <a href="/wiki/Assyrian_genocide" class="mw-redirect" title="Assyrian genocide">Assyrians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Greek_genocide" title="Greek genocide">Greeks</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Bloxham2005_130-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bloxham2005-130">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Levene_131-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Levene-131">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ferguson_132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ferguson-132">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> The share of non-Muslims in area within Turkey's current borders declined from 20-22% in 1914, or about 3.3.–3.6 million people, to around 3% in 1927.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the <a href="/wiki/Armistice_of_Mudros" title="Armistice of Mudros">Armistice of Mudros</a> on 30 October 1918, the victorious <a href="/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I" title="Allies of World War I">Allied Powers</a> sought to <a href="/wiki/Partitioning_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Partitioning of the Ottoman Empire">partition the Ottoman state</a> through the 1920 <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_S%C3%A8vres" title="Treaty of Sèvres">Treaty of Sèvres</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Treaty_of_Sèvres_134-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Treaty_of_Sèvres-134">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Republic_of_Turkey">Republic of Turkey</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="History of the Republic of Turkey">History of the Republic of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:252px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg/250px-Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="173" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg/375px-Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg/500px-Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg 2x" data-file-width="780" data-file-height="540" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Ataturk_and_Fethi_Okyar.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Mustafa_Kemal_Atat%C3%BCrk" title="Mustafa Kemal Atatürk">Mustafa Kemal Atatürk</a>, founder and first President of the Turkish Republic, with the <a href="/wiki/Liberal_Republican_Party_(Turkey)" title="Liberal Republican Party (Turkey)">Liberal Republican Party</a> leader <a href="/wiki/Fethi_Okyar" title="Fethi Okyar">Fethi Okyar</a> (right) and Nermin Kırdar (Fethi Okyar's daughter) in <a href="/wiki/Yalova" title="Yalova">Yalova</a>, 13 August 1930.</div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Occupation_of_Constantinople" class="mw-redirect" title="Occupation of Constantinople">occupation of Istanbul</a> (1918) and <a href="/wiki/Occupation_of_Smyrna" title="Occupation of Smyrna">İzmir</a> (1919) by the Allies in the aftermath of World War I prompted the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_National_Movement" title="Turkish National Movement">Turkish National Movement</a>. Under the leadership of <a href="/wiki/Mustafa_Kemal_Pasha" class="mw-redirect" title="Mustafa Kemal Pasha">Mustafa Kemal Pasha</a>, a military commander who had distinguished himself during the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Gallipoli" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Gallipoli">Battle of Gallipoli</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_War_of_Independence" title="Turkish War of Independence">Turkish War of Independence</a> (1919–1923) was waged with the aim of revoking the terms of the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_S%C3%A8vres" title="Treaty of Sèvres">Treaty of Sèvres</a> (1920).<sup id="cite_ref-Atatürk_135-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Atatürk-135">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>By 18 September 1922 the Greek, Armenian and French armies had been expelled,<sup id="cite_ref-18sep1922_136-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18sep1922-136">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Provisional_Government" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Provisional Government">Turkish Provisional Government</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a>, which had declared itself the legitimate government of the country on <a href="/wiki/Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey" title="Grand National Assembly of Turkey">23 April 1920</a>, started to formalise the legal transition from the old Ottoman into the new Republican political system. On 1 November 1922, the Turkish Parliament in Ankara formally <a href="/wiki/Abolition_of_the_Ottoman_Sultanate" class="mw-redirect" title="Abolition of the Ottoman Sultanate">abolished the Sultanate</a>, thus ending 623 years of monarchical Ottoman rule. The <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Lausanne" title="Treaty of Lausanne">Treaty of Lausanne</a> of 24 July 1923, which superseded the Treaty of Sèvres,<sup id="cite_ref-Treaty_of_Sèvres_134-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Treaty_of_Sèvres-134">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Atatürk_135-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Atatürk-135">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> led to the international recognition of the sovereignty of the newly formed "Republic of Turkey" as the successor state of the Ottoman Empire, and the republic was officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital.<sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Convention_Concerning_the_Exchange_of_Greek_and_Turkish_Populations" title="Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations">Lausanne Convention</a> stipulated a <a href="/wiki/Population_exchange_between_Greece_and_Turkey" title="Population exchange between Greece and Turkey">population exchange between Greece and Turkey</a>, whereby 1.1&#160;million Greeks left Turkey for Greece in exchange for 380,000 Muslims transferred from Greece to Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-Clogg_138-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clogg-138">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:232px;"><a href="/wiki/File:First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_(1935).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg/230px-First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="230" height="176" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg/345px-First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg/460px-First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_%281935%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1067" data-file-height="815" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:First_female_MPs_of_the_Turkish_Parliament_(1935).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Eighteen female <a href="/wiki/Member_of_parliament" title="Member of parliament">deputies</a> joined the <a href="/wiki/Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey" title="Grand National Assembly of Turkey">Turkish Parliament</a> with the <a href="/wiki/1935_Turkish_general_election" title="1935 Turkish general election">1935 general elections</a>. Turkish women gained the <a href="/wiki/Timeline_of_women%27s_suffrage" title="Timeline of women&#39;s suffrage">right to vote and to hold elected office</a> as a mark of the far-reaching <a href="/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk%27s_Reforms" class="mw-redirect" title="Atatürk&#39;s Reforms">social changes</a> initiated by <a href="/wiki/Mustafa_Kemal_Atat%C3%BCrk" title="Mustafa Kemal Atatürk">Atatürk</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Mustafa Kemal became the republic's first <a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">President</a> and subsequently introduced <a href="/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk%27s_Reforms" class="mw-redirect" title="Atatürk&#39;s Reforms">many reforms</a>. The reforms aimed to transform the old <a href="/wiki/Millet_(Ottoman_Empire)" title="Millet (Ottoman Empire)">religion-based and multi-communal</a> Ottoman <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy" title="Constitutional monarchy">constitutional monarchy</a> into a Turkish <a href="/wiki/Nation_state" title="Nation state">nation state</a> that would be governed as a <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_republic" title="Parliamentary republic">parliamentary republic</a> under a <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Constitution_of_1924" title="Turkish Constitution of 1924">secular constitution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-BoweringCrone2012_140-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BoweringCrone2012-140">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup> With the <a href="/wiki/Surname_Law" class="mw-redirect" title="Surname Law">Surname Law</a> of 1934, the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Parliament" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Parliament">Turkish Parliament</a> bestowed upon Mustafa Kemal the honorific surname "Atatürk" (<i>Father Turk</i>).<sup id="cite_ref-Atatürk_135-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Atatürk-135">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Montreux_Convention_Regarding_the_Regime_of_the_Straits" title="Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits">Montreux Convention</a> (1936) restored Turkey's control over the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Straits" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Straits">Turkish Straits</a>, including the right to militarise the coastlines of the <a href="/wiki/Dardanelles" title="Dardanelles">Dardanelles</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bosporus" title="Bosporus">Bosporus</a> straits and the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Marmara" title="Sea of Marmara">Sea of Marmara</a>, and to block maritime traffic in wartime.<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the establishment of the Republic of Turkey in 1923, some <a href="/wiki/Kurds" title="Kurds">Kurdish</a> and <a href="/wiki/Zazas" title="Zazas">Zaza</a> tribes, which were <a href="/wiki/Feudalism" title="Feudalism">feudal</a> (<a href="/wiki/Manorialism" title="Manorialism">manorial</a>) communities led by <a href="/wiki/Tribal_chief" title="Tribal chief">chieftains</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Agha_(title)" title="Agha (title)">agha</a></i>) during the Ottoman period, became discontent about certain aspects of <a href="/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk%27s_Reforms" class="mw-redirect" title="Atatürk&#39;s Reforms">Atatürk's reforms</a> aiming to modernise the country, such as <a href="/wiki/Secularism" title="Secularism">secularism</a> (the <a href="/wiki/Sheikh_Said_rebellion" title="Sheikh Said rebellion">Sheikh Said rebellion</a>, 1925)<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Land_reform" title="Land reform">land reform</a> (the <a href="/wiki/Dersim_rebellion" title="Dersim rebellion">Dersim rebellion</a>, 1937–1938),<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> and staged armed revolts that were put down with military operations.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/%C4%B0smet_%C4%B0n%C3%B6n%C3%BC" title="İsmet İnönü">İsmet İnönü</a> became Turkey's second President following Atatürk's death on 10 November 1938. On 29 June 1939, the <a href="/wiki/Hatay_State" title="Hatay State">Republic of Hatay</a> voted in favour of joining Turkey with a referendum. Turkey <a href="/wiki/Second_Cairo_Conference" title="Second Cairo Conference">remained neutral</a> during most of <a href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</a>, but entered the closing stages of the war on the side of the <a href="/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II" title="Allies of World War II">Allies</a> on 23 February 1945. On 26 June 1945, Turkey became a <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Charter" class="mw-redirect" title="United Nations Charter">charter member</a> of the United Nations.<sup id="cite_ref-Turkey_UN_144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Turkey_UN-144">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> In the following year, the <a href="/wiki/One-party_period_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="One-party period of the Republic of Turkey">one-party period</a> in Turkey came to an end, with the <a href="/wiki/1946_Turkish_general_election" title="1946 Turkish general election">first multi-party elections in 1946</a>. In 1950 Turkey became a member of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a>.
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:252px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg/250px-Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="200" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg/375px-Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg/500px-Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1512" data-file-height="1209" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Roosevelt_In%C3%B6n%C3%BC_and_Churchill_in_Cairo_cph.3b15312.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt" title="Franklin D. Roosevelt">Roosevelt</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C4%B0smet_%C4%B0n%C3%B6n%C3%BC" title="İsmet İnönü">İnönü</a> and <a href="/wiki/Winston_Churchill" title="Winston Churchill">Churchill</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Second_Cairo_Conference" title="Second Cairo Conference">Second Cairo Conference</a>, 1943.</div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Democrat_Party_(Turkey,_1946%E2%80%931961)" title="Democrat Party (Turkey, 1946–1961)">Democrat Party</a> established by <a href="/wiki/Cel%C3%A2l_Bayar" title="Celâl Bayar">Celâl Bayar</a> won the <a href="/wiki/1950_Turkish_general_election" title="1950 Turkish general election">1950</a>, <a href="/wiki/1954_Turkish_general_election" title="1954 Turkish general election">1954</a> and <a href="/wiki/1957_Turkish_general_election" title="1957 Turkish general election">1957</a> general elections and stayed in power for a decade, with <a href="/wiki/Adnan_Menderes" title="Adnan Menderes">Adnan Menderes</a> as the Prime Minister and Bayar as the President. After fighting as part of the United Nations forces in the <a href="/wiki/Korean_War" title="Korean War">Korean War</a>, Turkey joined <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a> in 1952, becoming a bulwark against Soviet expansion into the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Basin" title="Mediterranean Basin">Mediterranean</a>. Turkey subsequently became a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development" class="mw-redirect" title="Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development">OECD</a> in 1961, and an <a href="/wiki/Ankara_Agreement" title="Ankara Agreement">associate member</a> of the <a href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">EEC</a> in 1963.<sup id="cite_ref-oecd.org_145-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-oecd.org-145">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The country's tumultuous transition to <a href="/wiki/Multi-party_period_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="Multi-party period of the Republic of Turkey">multi-party democracy</a> was interrupted by military <a href="/wiki/Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="Coup d&#39;état">coups d'état</a> in <a href="/wiki/1960_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1960 Turkish coup d&#39;état">1960</a> and <a href="/wiki/1980_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1980 Turkish coup d&#39;état">1980</a>, as well as by military memorandums in <a href="/wiki/1971_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" class="mw-redirect" title="1971 Turkish coup d&#39;état">1971</a> and <a href="/wiki/1997_military_memorandum_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="1997 military memorandum (Turkey)">1997</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-TRPoliticsandMilitary_146-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TRPoliticsandMilitary-146">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup> Between 1960 and the end of the 20th century, the prominent leaders in Turkish politics who achieved multiple election victories were <a href="/wiki/S%C3%BCleyman_Demirel" title="Süleyman Demirel">Süleyman Demirel</a>, <a href="/wiki/B%C3%BClent_Ecevit" title="Bülent Ecevit">Bülent Ecevit</a> and <a href="/wiki/Turgut_%C3%96zal" title="Turgut Özal">Turgut Özal</a>. <a href="/wiki/Tansu_%C3%87iller" title="Tansu Çiller">Tansu Çiller</a> became the first female prime minister of Turkey in 1993.
</p><p>Following a decade of <a href="/wiki/Cypriot_intercommunal_violence" title="Cypriot intercommunal violence">Cypriot intercommunal violence</a> and the <a href="/wiki/1974_Cypriot_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1974 Cypriot coup d&#39;état">coup in Cyprus on 15 July 1974</a> staged by the <a href="/wiki/EOKA_B" title="EOKA B">EOKA B</a> paramilitary organisation, which overthrew President <a href="/wiki/Makarios_III" title="Makarios III">Makarios</a> and installed the pro-<a href="/wiki/Enosis" title="Enosis">Enosis</a> (union with Greece) <a href="/wiki/Nikos_Sampson" title="Nikos Sampson">Nikos Sampson</a> as dictator, <a href="/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus" title="Turkish invasion of Cyprus">Turkey invaded Cyprus</a> on 20 July 1974 by unilaterally exercising Article IV in the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Guarantee_(1960)" title="Treaty of Guarantee (1960)">Treaty of Guarantee (1960)</a>, but without restoring the <a href="/wiki/Status_quo_ante_bellum" title="Status quo ante bellum">status quo ante</a> at the end of the military operation.<sup id="cite_ref-Uslu2003_148-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Uslu2003-148">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> In 1983 the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Republic_of_Northern_Cyprus" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus">Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus</a>, which is recognised only by Turkey, was established.<sup id="cite_ref-trnc_149-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-trnc-149">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Annan_Plan_for_Cyprus" class="mw-redirect" title="Annan Plan for Cyprus">Annan Plan</a> for reunifying the island was supported by the majority of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Cypriots" title="Turkish Cypriots">Turkish Cypriots</a>, but rejected by the majority of <a href="/wiki/Greek_Cypriots" title="Greek Cypriots">Greek Cypriots</a>, in separate <a href="/wiki/2004_Cypriot_Annan_Plan_referendums" title="2004 Cypriot Annan Plan referendums">referendums in 2004</a>. However, negotiations for solving the <a href="/wiki/Cyprus_dispute" class="mw-redirect" title="Cyprus dispute">Cyprus dispute</a> are still ongoing between Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot political leaders.<sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Kurdish%E2%80%93Turkish_conflict_(1978%E2%80%93present)" title="Kurdish–Turkish conflict (1978–present)">conflict</a> between Turkey and the <a href="/wiki/Kurdistan_Workers%27_Party" title="Kurdistan Workers&#39; Party">Kurdistan Workers' Party</a> (PKK) (designated a <a href="/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups" title="List of designated terrorist groups">terrorist organisation</a> by Turkey, the United States,<sup id="cite_ref-department-of-state-list_151-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-department-of-state-list-151">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a><sup id="cite_ref-european-council-list_152-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-european-council-list-152">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup>) has been active since 1984, primarily in the southeast of the country. More than 40,000 people have died as a result of the conflict.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> In 1999 PKK's founder <a href="/wiki/Abdullah_%C3%96calan" title="Abdullah Öcalan">Abdullah Öcalan</a> was arrested and sentenced for <a href="/wiki/Terrorism" title="Terrorism">terrorism</a><sup id="cite_ref-department-of-state-list_151-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-department-of-state-list-151">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-european-council-list_152-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-european-council-list-152">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Treason" title="Treason">treason</a> charges.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc-29-06-1999_156-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc-29-06-1999-156">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bbc-03-10-2002_157-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc-03-10-2002-157">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> In the past, various <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Kurdish people">Kurdish</a> groups have unsuccessfully sought <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_separatism" class="mw-redirect" title="Ethnic separatism">separation</a> from Turkey to create an independent <a href="/wiki/Kurdistan" title="Kurdistan">Kurdish state</a>, while others have more recently pursued provincial <a href="/wiki/Autonomy" title="Autonomy">autonomy</a> and greater <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_of_Kurdish_people_in_Turkey" title="Human rights of Kurdish people in Turkey">political and cultural rights</a> for Kurds in Turkey. In the 21st century some reforms have taken place to improve the cultural rights of ethnic minorities in Turkey, such as the establishment of <a href="/wiki/TRT_Kurd%C3%AE" title="TRT Kurdî">TRT Kurdî</a>, <a href="/wiki/TRT_Arabi" title="TRT Arabi">TRT Arabi</a> and <a href="/wiki/TRT_Avaz" title="TRT Avaz">TRT Avaz</a> by the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Radio_and_Television_Corporation" title="Turkish Radio and Television Corporation">TRT</a>.
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:257px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg/255px-Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg" decoding="async" width="255" height="128" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg/383px-Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg/510px-Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg 2x" data-file-width="7594" data-file-height="3797" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Ankara_asv2021-10_img04_An%C4%B1tkabir.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/An%C4%B1tkabir" title="Anıtkabir">Anıtkabir</a>, the mausoleum of <a href="/wiki/Mustafa_Kemal_Atat%C3%BCrk" title="Mustafa Kemal Atatürk">Mustafa Kemal Atatürk</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a>, is visited by large crowds every year during national holidays, such as Republic Day on 29 October.</div></div></div>
<p>Since the liberalisation of the Turkish economy in the 1980s, the country has enjoyed stronger economic growth and greater political stability.<sup id="cite_ref-80sLiberalization_158-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80sLiberalization-158">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup> Turkey applied for full membership of the EEC in 1987, joined the <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Customs_Union" title="European Union Customs Union">EU Customs Union</a> in 1995 and started <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Turkey_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Turkey to the European Union">accession negotiations</a> with the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> in 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-TR_EUChrono_159-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TR_EUChrono-159">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-barroso_160-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-barroso-160">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> In a non-binding vote on 13 March 2019, the <a href="/wiki/European_Parliament" title="European Parliament">European Parliament</a> called on the EU governments to suspend EU accession talks with Turkey, citing violations of human rights and the rule of law; but the negotiations, effectively on hold since 2018, remain active as of 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-dw-13-03-2019_161-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dw-13-03-2019-161">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2013, <a href="/wiki/2013_protests_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="2013 protests in Turkey">widespread protests</a> erupted in many Turkish provinces, sparked by a plan to demolish <a href="/wiki/Gezi_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Gezi Park">Gezi Park</a> but soon growing into general anti-government dissent.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> In August 2014, Turkish Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan won Turkey's first direct presidential <a href="/wiki/2014_Turkish_presidential_election" title="2014 Turkish presidential election">election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> On 15 July 2016, an <a href="/wiki/2016_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat_attempt" title="2016 Turkish coup d&#39;état attempt">unsuccessful coup attempt</a> tried to oust the government.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup> As a reaction to the failed coup d'état, the government carried out <a href="/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Turkish_purges" class="mw-redirect" title="2016–17 Turkish purges">mass purges</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes.comxx_165-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes.comxx-165">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> jailed journalists, and shut down media outlets.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> In April 2017, the constitutional amendments, which significantly increased the powers of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, were narrowly accepted in the <a href="/wiki/2017_Turkish_constitutional_referendum" title="2017 Turkish constitutional referendum">constitutional referendum</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup> In June 2018, President Erdogan  was re-elected for a new five-year term in the first round of the <a href="/wiki/2018_Turkish_presidential_election" title="2018 Turkish presidential election">presidential election</a>. His AK Party (AKP) secured a majority in the separate <a href="/wiki/2018_Turkish_parliamentary_election" title="2018 Turkish parliamentary election">parliamentary election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Turkey" title="Administrative divisions of Turkey">Administrative divisions of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Regions_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Regions of Turkey">Regions of Turkey</a> and <a href="/wiki/NUTS_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="NUTS of Turkey">NUTS of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:252px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg/250px-Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="161" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg/375px-Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg/500px-Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3883" data-file-height="2508" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Ankara_from_bus_station.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a> is the capital of Turkey and the country's second largest city.</div></div></div>
<p>Turkey has a <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary</a> structure in terms of administration and this aspect is one of the most important factors shaping the Turkish public administration. Turkey does not have a <a href="/wiki/Federalism" title="Federalism">federal</a> system, and the provinces are subordinate to the <a href="/wiki/Central_government" title="Central government">central government</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a>.
</p><p>When three powers (executive, legislative and judiciary) are taken into account as the main functions of the state, local administrations have little power. Local administrations were established to provide services in place and the government is represented by the province governors (<i>vali</i>) and town governors (<i>kaymakam</i>). 
</p><p>Other senior public officials are also appointed by the central government, except for the mayors (<i>belediye başkanı</i>) who are elected by the constituents.<sup id="cite_ref-justice.gov.tr_170-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-justice.gov.tr-170">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> Turkish municipalities have local legislative bodies (<i>belediye meclisi</i>) for decision-making on municipal issues.
</p><p>Within this unitary framework, Turkey is subdivided into 81 <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_Turkey" title="Provinces of Turkey">provinces</a> (<i>il</i> or <i>vilayet</i>) for administrative purposes. Each province is divided into <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Turkey" title="Districts of Turkey">districts</a> (<i>ilçe</i>), for a total of 973 districts.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> Turkey is also subdivided into 7 <a href="/wiki/Geographical_regions_of_Turkey" title="Geographical regions of Turkey">regions</a> (<i>bölge</i>) and 21 subregions for geographic, demographic and economic purposes; this does not refer to an administrative division.
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_and_politics">Government and politics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Turkey" title="Government of Turkey">Government of Turkey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Turkey" title="Politics of Turkey">Politics of Turkey</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Turkey" title="Constitution of Turkey">Constitution of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:242px;max-width:242px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:240px;max-width:240px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:107px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:TBMM,_October_2021.jpg" class="image"><img alt="The Parliament of Turkey" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg/238px-TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg" decoding="async" width="238" height="107" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg/357px-TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg/476px-TBMM%2C_October_2021.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="1816" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">The <a href="/wiki/Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey" title="Grand National Assembly of Turkey">Grand National Assembly</a>,<br /> the <a href="/wiki/Legislative_chamber" title="Legislative chamber">legislative chamber</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:240px;max-width:240px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:126px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg" class="image"><img alt="The Presidential Complex" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg/238px-Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg" decoding="async" width="238" height="127" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg/357px-Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg/476px-Presidential_Palace_Main.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3399" data-file-height="1807" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">The <a href="/wiki/Presidential_Complex_(Turkey)" title="Presidential Complex (Turkey)">Presidential Complex</a>, residence and workplace of the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">President of Turkey</a></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:240px;max-width:240px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:133px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="The Court of Cassation" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg/238px-Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg" decoding="async" width="238" height="134" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg/357px-Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg/476px-Court_of_Cassation_in_Ankara2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2268" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">The <a href="/wiki/Court_of_Cassation_(Turkey)" title="Court of Cassation (Turkey)">Court of Cassation</a> is Turkey's <a href="/wiki/Supreme_court" title="Supreme court">supreme court</a> for reviewing verdicts given by courts of criminal and civil justice.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is a <a href="/wiki/Presidential_system" title="Presidential system">presidential</a> <a href="/wiki/Republic" title="Republic">republic</a> within a <a href="/wiki/Multi-party_period_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="Multi-party period of the Republic of Turkey">multi-party system</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-CIAFactbookTurkey_172-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CIAFactbookTurkey-172">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Turkey" title="Constitution of Turkey">current constitution</a> was approved by <a href="/wiki/1982_Turkish_constitutional_referendum" title="1982 Turkish constitutional referendum">referendum in 1982</a>, which determines the government's structure, lays forth the ideals and standards of the state's conduct, and&#160;sets&#160;out the state's responsibility to its citizens. Furthermore, the constitution specifies the people's rights and obligations, as well as principles for the delegation and exercise of sovereignty that belongs to the people of Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup> Turkish politics have become increasingly associated with <a href="/wiki/Democratic_backsliding" title="Democratic backsliding">democratic backsliding</a>, being described as a <a href="/wiki/Hybrid_regime" title="Hybrid regime">competitive authoritarian</a> system,<sup id="cite_ref-Esen_Gumuscu_2020_pp._1075–1091_174-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Esen_Gumuscu_2020_pp._1075–1091-174">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Borsuk_Levin_2021_pp._175–187_175-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Borsuk_Levin_2021_pp._175–187-175">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Cavatorta_Storm_Resta_2020_p._248_176-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cavatorta_Storm_Resta_2020_p._248-176">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup> with the government <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Turkey" title="Human rights in Turkey">restricting fundamental freedoms and compromising the rule of law</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Human_Rights_Watch_2021_177-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Human_Rights_Watch_2021-177">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the Turkish <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary system</a>, citizens are subject to <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Turkey" title="Administrative divisions of Turkey">three levels of government</a>: national, provincial, and local. The <a href="/wiki/Local_government" title="Local government">local government</a>'s duties are commonly split between <a href="/wiki/Municipal_corporation" title="Municipal corporation">municipal governments</a> and <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Turkey" title="Districts of Turkey">districts</a>, in which the executive and legislative officials are elected by a <a href="/wiki/Plurality_voting_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Plurality voting system">plurality vote</a> of citizens by district. Turkey is subdivided into <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_Turkey" title="Provinces of Turkey">81 provinces</a> for administrative purposes. Each province is divided into districts, for a total of <a href="/wiki/List_of_districts_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="List of districts in Turkey">973 districts</a>.
</p><p>The government, regulated by a system of <a href="/wiki/Separation_of_powers" title="Separation of powers">separation of powers</a> as defined by the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Turkey" title="Constitution of Turkey">constitution of Turkey</a>, comprises three branches:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Legislature" title="Legislature">Legislative</a>: The <a href="/wiki/Unicameralism" title="Unicameralism">unicameral</a> <a href="/wiki/Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey" title="Grand National Assembly of Turkey">Parliament</a> makes <a href="/wiki/Law" title="Law">laws</a>, debates and adopts the budget bills, <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_war" title="Declaration of war">declares war</a>, approves treaties, proclaims <a href="/wiki/Amnesty" title="Amnesty">amnesty</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pardon" title="Pardon">pardon</a>, and has the power of <a href="/wiki/Impeachment" title="Impeachment">impeachment</a>, by which it can remove incumbent members of the government.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Executive_(government)" title="Executive (government)">Executive</a>: <a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">The president</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Commander-in-chief" title="Commander-in-chief">commander-in-chief</a> of the military, can veto <a href="/wiki/Bill_(law)" title="Bill (law)">legislative bills</a> before they become law (subject to parliamentary override), can issue <a href="/wiki/Decree" title="Decree">presidential decrees</a> on matters regarding executive power with the exception of fundamental rights, individual rights and certain political rights (parliamentary laws prevail presidential decrees), and appoints the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Turkey" title="Cabinet of Turkey">members of the Cabinet</a> and other officers, who administer and enforce national laws and policies.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Judiciary" title="Judiciary">Judicial</a>: The <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Turkey" title="Constitutional Court of Turkey">Constitutional Court</a> (for <a href="/wiki/Constitutionality" title="Constitutionality">constitutional adjudication</a> and review of individual applications concerning human rights), the <a href="/wiki/Court_of_Cassation_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Court of Cassation of Turkey">Court of Cassation</a> (final decision maker in ordinary judiciary), the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Council_of_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Council of State">Council of State</a> (final decision maker in administrative judiciary) and the <a href="/wiki/Court_of_Jurisdictional_Disputes" title="Court of Jurisdictional Disputes">Court of Jurisdictional Disputes</a> (for resolving the disputes between courts for constitutional jurisdiction) are the four organizations that are described by the Constitution as supreme courts. The judges of the Constitutional Court are appointed by the president and the parliament.<sup id="cite_ref-Constitution2019_5-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Constitution2019-5">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>
<p>The Parliament has 600 voting members, each representing a <a href="/wiki/Constituency" class="mw-redirect" title="Constituency">constituency</a> for a five-year term. Parliamentary seats are distributed among the provinces by population, conforming with the census apportionment. The president is <a href="/wiki/Turkish_presidential_elections" title="Turkish presidential elections">elected</a> by <a href="/wiki/Direct_vote" class="mw-redirect" title="Direct vote">direct vote</a> and serves a five-year term. The president can't run for re-elections after two terms of five-years, unless the parliament prematurely renews the presidential elections during the second term of the President. Elections for the Parliament and presidential elections are held on the same day. The Constitutional Court is composed of fifteen members. A member is elected for a term of twelve years and can't be re-elected. The members of the Constitutional Court are obliged to retire when they are over the age of sixty-five.<sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Parties_and_elections">Parties and elections</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Turkey" title="Elections in Turkey">Elections in Turkey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Political_parties_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Political parties in Turkey">Political parties in Turkey</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Electoral_cycle_of_Turkey" title="Electoral cycle of Turkey">Electoral cycle of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright" style=""><div class="thumbinner" style="width:162px"><div class="thumbimage noresize" style="width:160px;">
<a href="/wiki/File:Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ukraine.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg/160px-Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg" decoding="async" width="160" height="214" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg/240px-Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg/320px-Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_in_Ukraine.jpg 2x" data-file-width="570" data-file-height="763" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><div style="text-align:center;"><a href="/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan" title="Recep Tayyip Erdoğan">Recep Tayyip Erdoğan</a><br /><small><a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">President</a></small></div></div></div></div>
<p>Elections in Turkey are held for six functions of <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Turkey" title="Government of Turkey">government</a>: <a href="/wiki/Turkish_presidential_elections" title="Turkish presidential elections">presidential elections</a> (national), <a href="/wiki/Grand_National_Assembly_of_Turkey" title="Grand National Assembly of Turkey">parliamentary elections</a> (national), <a href="/wiki/Metropolitan_municipalities_in_Turkey" title="Metropolitan municipalities in Turkey">municipality mayors</a> (local), <a href="/wiki/List_of_districts_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="List of districts in Turkey">district mayors</a> (local), <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_Turkey" title="Provinces of Turkey">provincial</a> or <a href="/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Turkey" title="List of municipalities in Turkey">municipal council members</a> (local) and <a href="/wiki/Muhtar_(title)" title="Muhtar (title)">muhtars</a> (local). Apart from elections, <a href="/wiki/Referendum" title="Referendum">referendums</a> are also held occasionally.
</p><p>Every Turkish citizen who has turned 18 has the <a href="/wiki/Suffrage" title="Suffrage">right to vote</a> and stand as a candidate at elections. <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">Universal suffrage</a> for both sexes has been applied throughout Turkey since 1934 and before most countries. In Turkey, <a href="/wiki/Voter_turnout" title="Voter turnout">turnout rates</a> of both local and general elections are high compared to many other countries, which usually stands higher than 80 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> There are 600 <a href="/wiki/Member_of_Parliament" class="mw-redirect" title="Member of Parliament">members of parliament</a> who are elected for a five-year term by a <a href="/wiki/Party-list_proportional_representation" title="Party-list proportional representation">party-list proportional representation</a> system from 88 electoral districts. 
The Constitutional Court can strip the public financing of <a href="/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Turkey" title="List of political parties in Turkey">political parties</a> that it deems <a href="/wiki/Secularism_in_Turkey" title="Secularism in Turkey">anti-secular</a> or having ties to <a href="/wiki/Terrorism_in_Turkey" title="Terrorism in Turkey">terrorism</a>, or ban their existence altogether.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Electoral_threshold" title="Electoral threshold">electoral threshold</a> for political parties at national level is seven percent of the votes.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> Smaller parties can avoid the electoral threshold by forming an <a href="/wiki/Political_alliance" class="mw-redirect" title="Political alliance">alliance</a> with other parties, in which it is sufficient that the total votes of the alliance passes 7%. <a href="/wiki/Independent_politician" title="Independent politician">Independent candidates</a> are not subject to an electoral threshold.
</p><p>After World War II, starting from 1946, Turkey operated under a <a href="/wiki/Multi-party_period_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="Multi-party period of the Republic of Turkey">multi-party system</a>. On the right side of the Turkish <a href="/wiki/Political_spectrum" title="Political spectrum">political spectrum</a>, parties like the <a href="/wiki/Democratic_Party_(Turkey,_historical)" class="mw-redirect" title="Democratic Party (Turkey, historical)">Democrat Party</a> (DP), <a href="/wiki/Justice_Party_(Turkey)" title="Justice Party (Turkey)">Justice Party</a> (AP), <a href="/wiki/Motherland_Party_(Turkey)" title="Motherland Party (Turkey)">Motherland Party</a> (ANAP) and <a href="/wiki/Justice_and_Development_Party_(Turkey)" title="Justice and Development Party (Turkey)">Justice and Development Party</a> (AKP) became the most popular political parties in Turkey, winning numerous elections. Turkish <a href="/wiki/Right-wing_politics" title="Right-wing politics">right-wing</a> parties are more likely to embrace the principles of political ideologies such as <a href="/wiki/Conservatism" title="Conservatism">conservatism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nationalism" title="Nationalism">nationalism</a> or <a href="/wiki/Islamism" title="Islamism">Islamism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> On the left side of the spectrum, parties like the <a href="/wiki/Republican_People%27s_Party" title="Republican People&#39;s Party">Republican People's Party</a> (CHP), <a href="/wiki/Social_Democratic_Populist_Party_(Turkey)" title="Social Democratic Populist Party (Turkey)">Social Democratic Populist Party</a> (SHP) and <a href="/wiki/Democratic_Left_Party_(Turkey)" title="Democratic Left Party (Turkey)">Democratic Left Party</a> (DSP) once enjoyed the largest electoral success. <a href="/wiki/Left-wing_politics" title="Left-wing politics">Left-wing</a> parties are more likely to embrace the principles of <a href="/wiki/Socialism" title="Socialism">socialism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kemalism" title="Kemalism">Kemalism</a> or <a href="/wiki/Secularism" title="Secularism">secularism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FleetFaroqhi2008p357_186-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FleetFaroqhi2008p357-186">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The 12th <a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">President</a>, <a href="/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan" title="Recep Tayyip Erdoğan">Recep Tayyip Erdoğan</a> (AKP), winner of the <a href="/wiki/2018_Turkish_presidential_election" title="2018 Turkish presidential election">2018 presidential election</a> and former <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Turkey" title="Prime Minister of Turkey">prime minister</a>, is currently serving as the <a href="/wiki/Head_of_state" title="Head of state">head of state</a> and <a href="/wiki/Head_of_government" title="Head of government">head of government</a>. <a href="/wiki/Kemal_K%C4%B1l%C4%B1%C3%A7daro%C4%9Flu" title="Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu">Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu</a> (CHP) is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_the_main_opposition_leaders_of_Turkey" title="List of the main opposition leaders of Turkey">main opposition leader</a> in Turkey. <a href="/wiki/Mustafa_%C5%9Eentop" title="Mustafa Şentop">Mustafa Şentop</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Speaker_of_the_Grand_National_Assembly" title="Speaker of the Grand National Assembly">Speaker of the Grand National Assembly</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/2018_Turkish_parliamentary_election" title="2018 Turkish parliamentary election">2018 parliamentary election</a> was held for voting into office the members of the <a href="/wiki/27th_Parliament_of_Turkey" title="27th Parliament of Turkey">27th Parliament of Turkey</a>, which had an initial composition of 295 seats for the <a href="/wiki/Justice_and_Development_Party_(Turkey)" title="Justice and Development Party (Turkey)">Justice and Development Party</a> (AKP), 146 seats for the <a href="/wiki/Republican_People%27s_Party" title="Republican People&#39;s Party">Republican People's Party</a> (CHP), 67 seats for the <a href="/wiki/Peoples%27_Democratic_Party_(Turkey)" title="Peoples&#39; Democratic Party (Turkey)">Peoples' Democratic Party</a> (HDP), 49 seats for the <a href="/wiki/Nationalist_Movement_Party" title="Nationalist Movement Party">Nationalist Movement Party</a> (MHP) and 49 seats for the <a href="/wiki/Good_Party" title="Good Party">Good Party</a> (İP).<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> The next parliamentary election is scheduled to take place in 2023.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Law">Law</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Judicial_system_of_Turkey" title="Judicial system of Turkey">Judicial system of Turkey</a> and <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Turkey" title="Law enforcement in Turkey">Law enforcement in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:242px;"><a href="/wiki/File:PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_(1).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg/240px-PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="159" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg/360px-PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg/480px-PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_%281%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3752" data-file-height="2486" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:PalaceOfJusticeIstanbul_(1).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Istanbul Justice Palace in the Şişli district on the European side</div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:242px;"><a href="/wiki/File:%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg/240px-%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="135" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg/360px-%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg/480px-%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2268" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:%C4%B0stanbulAnadoluJusticePalace2.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Istanbul Anadolu Justice Palace in the Kartal district on the Asian side</div></div></div>
