<p>With the founding of the Republic, Turkey adopted a <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</a> legal system, replacing <a href="/wiki/Sharia" title="Sharia">Sharia</a>-derived <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_law" title="Ottoman law">Ottoman law</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_civil_code_(1926)" title="Turkish civil code (1926)">Civil Code</a>, adopted in 1926, was based on the <a href="/wiki/Swiss_Civil_Code" title="Swiss Civil Code">Swiss Civil Code</a> of 1907 and the <a href="/wiki/Swiss_Code_of_Obligations" title="Swiss Code of Obligations">Swiss Code of Obligations</a> of 1911. Although it underwent a number of changes in 2002, it retains much of the basis of the original Code. The <a href="/wiki/Criminal_Code" class="mw-redirect" title="Criminal Code">Criminal Code</a>, originally based on the <a href="/wiki/Italian_law_codes#Penal_Code" title="Italian law codes">Italian Criminal Code</a>, was replaced in 2005 by a Code with principles similar to the <a href="/wiki/German_Penal_Code" class="mw-redirect" title="German Penal Code">German Penal Code</a> and German law generally. <a href="/wiki/Administrative_law" title="Administrative law">Administrative law</a> is based on the French equivalent and <a href="/wiki/Procedural_law" title="Procedural law">procedural law</a> generally shows the influence of the Swiss, German and French legal systems.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup> Islamic principles do not play a part in the legal system.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Turkey has adopted the principle of the separation of powers. In line with this principle, judicial power is exercised by independent courts on behalf of the Turkish nation. The independence and organisation of the courts, the security of the tenure of judges and public prosecutors, the profession of judges and prosecutors, the supervision of judges and public prosecutors, the military courts and their organisation, and the powers and duties of the high courts are regulated by the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Constitution" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Constitution">Turkish Constitution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-uhdigm.adalet.gov.tr_190-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-uhdigm.adalet.gov.tr-190">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to Article 142 of the Turkish Constitution, the organisation, duties and jurisdiction of the courts, their functions and the trial procedures are regulated by law. In line with the aforementioned article of the Turkish Constitution and related laws, the court system in Turkey can be classified under three main categories; which are the Judicial Courts, Administrative Courts, and Military Courts. Each category includes first instance courts and high courts. In addition, the Court of Jurisdictional Disputes rules on cases that cannot be classified readily as falling within the purview of one court system.<sup id="cite_ref-uhdigm.adalet.gov.tr_190-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-uhdigm.adalet.gov.tr-190">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Turkey" title="Law enforcement in Turkey">Law enforcement in Turkey</a> is carried out by several agencies under the jurisdiction of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Interior_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of the Interior (Turkey)">Ministry of Internal Affairs</a>. These agencies are the <a href="/wiki/General_Directorate_of_Security_(Turkey)" title="General Directorate of Security (Turkey)">General Directorate of Security</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Gendarmerie_General_Command" title="Gendarmerie General Command">Gendarmerie General Command</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Coast_Guard_Command_(Turkey)" title="Coast Guard Command (Turkey)">Coast Guard Command</a>. Furthermore, there are other law enforcement agencies with specific (<a href="/wiki/National_Intelligence_Organization_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="National Intelligence Organization (Turkey)">National Intelligence Organization</a>, General Directorate of Customs Protection, etc.) or local (Village guards, Municipal Police, etc.) assignments that are under the jurisdiction of the president or different ministries.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (September 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>In the years of government by the AKP and Erdoğan, particularly since 2013, the independence and integrity of the Turkish judiciary has increasingly been said to be in doubt by institutions, parliamentarians and journalists both within and outside of Turkey; due to political interference in the promotion of judges and prosecutors, and in their pursuit of public duty.<sup id="cite_ref-EU2015_191-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EU2015-191">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-EP2016_192-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EP2016-192">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-TI2016_193-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TI2016-193">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup> The <i>Turkey 2015 report</i> of the <a href="/wiki/European_Commission" title="European Commission">European Commission</a> stated that "the independence of the judiciary and respect of the principle of separation of powers have been undermined and judges and prosecutors have been under strong political pressure."<sup id="cite_ref-EU2015_191-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EU2015-191">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Turkey" title="Foreign relations of Turkey">Foreign relations of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_(Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg/220px-Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="130" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg/330px-Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg/440px-Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_%28Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4227" data-file-height="2490" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Participants_at_the_2015_G20_Summit_(Presidencia_de_la_Naci%C3%B3n_Argentina).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/2015_G20_Antalya_summit" title="2015 G20 Antalya summit">2015 G20 Summit</a> held in <a href="/wiki/Antalya" title="Antalya">Antalya</a>, Turkey, a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a> (1961) and <a href="/wiki/G20" title="G20">G20</a> (1999).</div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/Turkey_and_the_United_Nations" title="Turkey and the United Nations">United Nations</a> (1945),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign3_195-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign3-195">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a> (1961),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign1_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign1-196">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation" title="Organisation of Islamic Cooperation">OIC</a> (1969),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign4_197-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign4-197">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe" title="Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe">OSCE</a> (1973),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign5_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign5-198">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Economic_Cooperation_Organization" title="Economic Cooperation Organization">ECO</a> (1985),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign6_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign6-199">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_the_Black_Sea_Economic_Cooperation" title="Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation">BSEC</a> (1992),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign7_200-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign7-200">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/International_Organization_of_Turkic_Culture" title="International Organization of Turkic Culture">TURKSOY</a> (1993), the <a href="/wiki/Developing_8_Countries" class="mw-redirect" title="Developing 8 Countries">D-8</a> (1997),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign8_201-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign8-201">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/G20" title="G20">G20</a> (1999),<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign2_202-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign2-202">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Turkic_States" title="Organization of Turkic States">OTS</a> (2009). Turkey was a member of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council" title="United Nations Security Council">United Nations Security Council</a> in 1951–1952, 1954–1955, 1961 and 2009–2010.<sup id="cite_ref-Hürriyet_UN_Security_203-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hürriyet_UN_Security-203">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup> In 2012 Turkey became a dialogue partner of the <a href="/wiki/Shanghai_Cooperation_Organisation" title="Shanghai Cooperation Organisation">SCO</a>, and in 2013 became a member of the <a href="/wiki/Asia_Cooperation_Dialogue" title="Asia Cooperation Dialogue">ACD</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AFGTUR_204-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AFGTUR-204">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-turkeyjoin_205-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-turkeyjoin-205">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In line with its traditional Western orientation, relations with Europe have always been a central part of Turkish foreign policy. Turkey became <a href="/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Council_of_Europe" title="Member states of the Council of Europe">one of the early members</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> in 1950, applied for associate membership of the <a href="/wiki/European_Economic_Community" title="European Economic Community">EEC</a> (predecessor of the European Union) in 1959 and became an <a href="/wiki/Ankara_Agreement" title="Ankara Agreement">associate member</a> in 1963. After decades of political negotiations, Turkey applied for full membership of the EEC in 1987, became an associate member of the <a href="/wiki/Western_European_Union" title="Western European Union">Western European Union</a> in 1992, joined the <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Customs_Union" title="European Union Customs Union">EU Customs Union</a> in 1995 and has been in <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Turkey_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Turkey to the European Union">formal accession negotiations</a> with the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> since 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-TR_EUChrono_159-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TR_EUChrono-159">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-barroso_160-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-barroso-160">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> 
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png/220px-EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="183" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png/330px-EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png/440px-EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="1000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:EU_and_Turkey_Locator_Map.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Turkey has been in <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Turkey_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Turkey to the European Union">formal accession negotiations</a> with the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> since 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-TR_EUChrono_159-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TR_EUChrono-159">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-barroso_160-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-barroso-160">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Turkey's support for <a href="/wiki/Northern_Cyprus" title="Northern Cyprus">Northern Cyprus</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Cyprus_dispute" class="mw-redirect" title="Cyprus dispute">Cyprus dispute</a> and refusal to include the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Cyprus" class="mw-redirect" title="Republic of Cyprus">Republic of Cyprus</a> to the <a href="/wiki/European_Union%E2%80%93Turkey_Customs_Union" title="European Union–Turkey Customs Union">EU-Turkey Customs Union agreement</a> complicates its relations with the European Union and remains a major stumbling block to the country's EU accession bid.<sup id="cite_ref-Mardell_206-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mardell-206">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Annan_Plan_for_Cyprus" class="mw-redirect" title="Annan Plan for Cyprus">Annan Plan</a> for the island's reunification was approved by the majority of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Cypriots" title="Turkish Cypriots">Turkish Cypriots</a>, but rejected by the majority of <a href="/wiki/Greek_Cypriots" title="Greek Cypriots">Greek Cypriots</a>, in separate <a href="/wiki/2004_Cypriot_Annan_Plan_referendums" title="2004 Cypriot Annan Plan referendums">referendums</a> on April 24, 2004. The Republic of Cyprus was admitted to the EU a week later, on May 1, 2004. According to the 1960 <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Guarantee_(1960)" title="Treaty of Guarantee (1960)">Treaty of Guarantee</a>, the United Kingdom, Greece and Turkey are the three guarantor states on the island.<sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The other defining aspect of Turkey's foreign policy has been the country's long-standing strategic alliance with the <a href="/wiki/Turkey%E2%80%93United_States_relations" title="Turkey–United States relations">United States</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-U.S.DoS-Turkey_208-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-U.S.DoS-Turkey-208">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-fas.org_209-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fas.org-209">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Truman_Doctrine" title="Truman Doctrine">Truman Doctrine</a> in 1947 enunciated American intentions to guarantee the security of Turkey and Greece during the <a href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</a>, and resulted in large-scale <a href="/wiki/Turkey-United_States_relations" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkey-United States relations">U.S. military and economic support</a>. In 1948 both countries were included in the <a href="/wiki/Marshall_Plan" title="Marshall Plan">Marshall Plan</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_for_European_Economic_Co-operation" class="mw-redirect" title="Organisation for European Economic Co-operation">OEEC</a> for rebuilding European economies.<sup id="cite_ref-Truman_Doctrine_210-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Truman_Doctrine-210">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The common threat posed by the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a> during the <a href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</a> led to Turkey's membership of <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a> in 1952, ensuring close bilateral relations with the US. Subsequently, Turkey benefited from the United States' political, economic and diplomatic support, including in key issues such as the country's bid to join the European Union.<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup> In the post–Cold War environment, Turkey's geostrategic importance shifted towards its proximity to the <a href="/wiki/Middle_East" title="Middle East">Middle East</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Caucasus" title="Caucasus">Caucasus</a> and the Balkans.<sup id="cite_ref-edoc.hu-berlin.de_212-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-edoc.hu-berlin.de-212">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup> 
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_(51246907423).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg/220px-%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg/330px-%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg/440px-%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_%2851246907423%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4802" data-file-height="3196" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:%D0%9D%D0%90%D0%A2%D0%9E_%D0%A1%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82_2021_NATO_Summit_2021_-14.06.2021-_(51246907423).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Armed_Forces" title="Turkish Armed Forces">Turkish Armed Forces</a> collectively rank as the second-largest standing military force in <a href="/wiki/Turkey_in_NATO" title="Turkey in NATO">NATO</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforeign_213-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforeign-213">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>The independence of the <a href="/wiki/Turkic_states" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkic states">Turkic states</a> of the Soviet Union in 1991, with which Turkey shares a common cultural, <a href="/wiki/Turkic_history" title="Turkic history">historic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Turkic_languages" title="Turkic languages">linguistic</a> heritage, allowed Turkey to extend its economic and political relations deep into <a href="/wiki/Central_Asia" title="Central Asia">Central Asia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Bal2004_214-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bal2004-214">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/International_Organization_of_Turkic_Culture" title="International Organization of Turkic Culture">International Organization of Turkic Culture</a> (TURKSOY) was established in 1993, and the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Turkic_States" title="Organization of Turkic States">Organization of Turkic States</a> (OTS) was established in 2009. The <a href="/wiki/Baku%E2%80%93Tbilisi%E2%80%93Ceyhan_pipeline" title="Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline">Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline</a>, a multi-billion-dollar oil and natural gas <a href="/wiki/Pipeline_transport" title="Pipeline transport">pipeline</a> that extends from <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a> in <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan" title="Azerbaijan">Azerbaijan</a> to the port of <a href="/wiki/Ceyhan" title="Ceyhan">Ceyhan</a> in Turkey, forms part of Turkey's foreign policy strategy to become an energy conduit from the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Sea" title="Caspian Sea">Caspian Sea</a> basin to Europe. Turkey sealed its land border with Armenia in a gesture of support to Azerbaijan (a Turkic state in the Caucasus region) during the <a href="/wiki/First_Nagorno-Karabakh_War" title="First Nagorno-Karabakh War">First</a> (1993) and <a href="/wiki/Second_Nagorno-Karabakh_War" title="Second Nagorno-Karabakh War">Second</a> (2020) Nagorno-Karabakh Wars, and it remains closed.<sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup> Armenia and Turkey started diplomatic talks in order to normalise the relationship between the two countries. The discussions include opening the closed borders and starting trade. Turkey and Armenia have also restarted commercial flights between the two countries.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Organization_of_Turkic_States_(orthographic_projection).svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/220px-Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="220" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/330px-Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/440px-Organization_of_Turkic_States_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="553" data-file-height="553" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Organization_of_Turkic_States_(orthographic_projection).svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Members and observers of the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Turkic_States" title="Organization of Turkic States">Organization of Turkic States</a></div></div></div> 
<p>Following the <a href="/wiki/Arab_Spring" title="Arab Spring">Arab Spring</a> in December 2010, the choices made by the AKP government for supporting certain political opposition groups in the affected countries have led to tensions with some Arab states, such as Turkey's neighbour Syria since the start of the <a href="/wiki/Syrian_civil_war" title="Syrian civil war">Syrian civil war</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a> after the <a href="/wiki/2013_Egyptian_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="2013 Egyptian coup d&#39;état">ousting of President Mohamed Morsi</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup> As of 2022<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Turkey&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, Turkey does not have an ambassador in either Syria or Egypt,<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup> but relations with both countries have started to improve.<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup> Diplomatic relations with <a href="/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Turkey_relations" title="Israel–Turkey relations">Israel</a> were also severed after the <a href="/wiki/Gaza_flotilla_raid" title="Gaza flotilla raid">Gaza flotilla raid</a> in 2010, but were normalised following a deal in June 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> These political rifts have left Turkey with few allies in the <a href="/wiki/Levant" title="Levant">East Mediterranean</a>, where large <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas" title="Natural gas">natural gas</a> fields have recently been discovered.<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> There is a dispute over Turkey's <a href="/wiki/Aegean_dispute" title="Aegean dispute">maritime boundaries with Greece</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cyprus%E2%80%93Turkey_maritime_zones_dispute" title="Cyprus–Turkey maritime zones dispute">Cyprus</a> and drilling rights in the eastern Mediterranean.<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After the <a href="/wiki/Russia%E2%80%93Turkey_relations#Normalisation_of_ties_and_beyond:_2016–present" title="Russia–Turkey relations">rapprochement with Russia</a> in 2016, Turkey revised its stance regarding the solution of the conflict in Syria.<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> In January 2018, the Turkish military and the Turkish-backed forces, including the <a href="/wiki/Syrian_National_Army" title="Syrian National Army">Syrian National Army</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup> began an <a href="/wiki/Operation_Olive_Branch" title="Operation Olive Branch">operation in Syria</a> aimed at ousting U.S.-backed <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units" class="mw-redirect" title="People&#39;s Protection Units">YPG</a> (which Turkey considers to be an offshoot of the outlawed <a href="/wiki/PKK" class="mw-redirect" title="PKK">PKK</a>)<sup id="cite_ref-Atlantic-Council_233-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Atlantic-Council-233">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup> from the enclave of <a href="/wiki/Afrin,_Syria" title="Afrin, Syria">Afrin</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-TRT-World-25-05-2022_236-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TRT-World-25-05-2022-236">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:272px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg/270px-Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg" decoding="async" width="270" height="203" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg/405px-Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg/540px-Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="3024" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Maquette_TF-X_Le_Bourget_2019.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/TAI_TF-X" title="TAI TF-X">TAI TF-X</a>, a twin-engined 5th generation air superiority fighter, is currently being produced by <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Aerospace_Industries" title="Turkish Aerospace Industries">Turkish Aerospace Industries</a>, with a planned roll-out date of March 18, 2023. <sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Armed_Forces" title="Turkish Armed Forces">Turkish Armed Forces</a> consist of the <a href="/wiki/General_Staff_of_the_Turkish_Armed_Forces" title="General Staff of the Turkish Armed Forces">General Staff</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Land_Forces" title="Turkish Land Forces">Land Forces</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Naval_Forces" title="Turkish Naval Forces">Naval Forces</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Air_Force" title="Turkish Air Force">Air Force</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Chief_of_the_Turkish_General_Staff" title="Chief of the Turkish General Staff">Chief of the General Staff</a> is appointed by the President. The President is responsible to the Parliament for matters of national security and the adequate preparation of the armed forces to defend the country. However, the authority to declare war and to deploy the Turkish Armed Forces to foreign countries or to allow foreign armed forces to be stationed in Turkey rests solely with the Parliament.<sup id="cite_ref-TSK_Organisation_242-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TSK_Organisation-242">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Gendarmerie" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Gendarmerie">Gendarmerie General Command</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Coast_Guard" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Coast Guard">Coast Guard Command</a> are law enforcement agencies with military organization (ranks, structure, etc.) and under the jurisdiction of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Interior_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of the Interior (Turkey)">Ministry of the Interior</a>. In wartime, the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Turkey" title="President of Turkey">president</a> can order certain units of the Gendarmerie General Command and the Coast Guard Command to operate under the Land Forces Command and Naval Forces Commands respectively. The remaining parts of the Gendarmerie and the Coast Guard continue to carry out their law enforcement missions under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Interior.
</p><p>Every fit male Turkish citizen otherwise not barred is required to <a href="/wiki/Conscription_in_Turkey" title="Conscription in Turkey">serve in the military</a> for a period ranging from three weeks to a year, dependent on education and job location.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> Turkey does not recognise <a href="/wiki/Conscientious_objector" title="Conscientious objector">conscientious objection</a> and does not offer a <a href="/wiki/Alternative_civilian_service" title="Alternative civilian service">civilian alternative</a> to military service.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Turkey has the <a href="/wiki/Member_states_of_NATO#Military_personnel" title="Member states of NATO">second-largest standing military force</a> in <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>, after the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces" title="United States Armed Forces">United States</a>, with an estimated strength of 890,700 military personnel as of February 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-iiss-mb-2022_245-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-iiss-mb-2022-245">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:322px;"><a href="/wiki/File:TCG_Anadolu.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/TCG_Anadolu.png/320px-TCG_Anadolu.png" decoding="async" width="320" height="180" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/TCG_Anadolu.png/480px-TCG_Anadolu.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/TCG_Anadolu.png/640px-TCG_Anadolu.png 2x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1080" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:TCG_Anadolu.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/TCG_Anadolu" title="TCG Anadolu">TCG <i>Anadolu</i> (L-400)</a> <a href="/wiki/Amphibious_assault_ship" title="Amphibious assault ship">amphibious assault ship</a> (<a href="/wiki/Landing_helicopter_dock" title="Landing helicopter dock">LHD</a> and <a href="/wiki/V/STOL" title="V/STOL">V/STOL</a> <a href="/wiki/Aircraft_carrier" title="Aircraft carrier">aircraft carrier</a>) of the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Navy" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Navy">Turkish Navy</a>. <a href="/wiki/Baykar_Bayraktar_K%C4%B1z%C4%B1lelma" title="Baykar Bayraktar Kızılelma">Baykar MIUS Kızılelma</a> is a jet-engined <a href="/wiki/UCAV" class="mw-redirect" title="UCAV">UCAV</a> designed to operate on TCG <i>Anadolu</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-Baykar_MIUS_Official_246-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Baykar_MIUS_Official-246">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup> Its maiden flight was successfully completed on December 14, 2022. <sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is one of five NATO member states which are part of the <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_sharing" title="Nuclear sharing">nuclear sharing</a> policy of the alliance, together with Belgium, <a href="/wiki/Germany_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Germany and weapons of mass destruction">Germany</a>, Italy, and the <a href="/wiki/Netherlands_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Netherlands and weapons of mass destruction">Netherlands</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> A total of 90 <a href="/wiki/B61_nuclear_bomb" title="B61 nuclear bomb">B61 nuclear bombs</a> are hosted at the <a href="/wiki/Incirlik_Air_Base" title="Incirlik Air Base">Incirlik Air Base</a>, 40 of which are allocated for use by the Turkish Air Force in case of a nuclear conflict, but their use requires the approval of NATO.<sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Turkey has participated in international missions under the United Nations and NATO <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Brigade" title="Turkish Brigade">since the Korean War</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Peacekeeping" title="Peacekeeping">peacekeeping</a> missions in <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Operation_in_Somalia_I" title="United Nations Operation in Somalia I">Somalia</a>, <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Protection_Force" title="United Nations Protection Force">Yugoslavia</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Operation_Ocean_Shield" title="Operation Ocean Shield">Horn of Africa</a>. It supported <a href="/wiki/Coalition_of_the_Gulf_War" title="Coalition of the Gulf War">coalition forces</a> in the <a href="/wiki/First_Gulf_War" class="mw-redirect" title="First Gulf War">First Gulf War</a>, contributed military personnel to the <a href="/wiki/International_Security_Assistance_Force" title="International Security Assistance Force">International Security Assistance Force</a> in Afghanistan, and remains active in <a href="/wiki/Kosovo_Force" title="Kosovo Force">Kosovo Force</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eurocorps" title="Eurocorps">Eurocorps</a> and <a href="/wiki/EU_Battlegroup" title="EU Battlegroup">EU Battlegroups</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Enter_the_EU_Battle_Groups_254-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Enter_the_EU_Battle_Groups-254">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-tskpeace_255-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tskpeace-255">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> In recent years, Turkey has assisted <a href="/wiki/Peshmerga" title="Peshmerga">Peshmerga</a> forces in northern <a href="/wiki/Iraq" title="Iraq">Iraq</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Somali_Armed_Forces" title="Somali Armed Forces">Somali Armed Forces</a> with security and training.<sup id="cite_ref-hurriyetdailynews.comq_256-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hurriyetdailynews.comq-256">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-reuters.comq_257-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters.comq-257">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>The Turkish Armed Forces have a relatively substantial military presence abroad,<sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup> with <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_with_overseas_military_bases" title="List of countries with overseas military bases">military bases</a> in <a href="/wiki/Pasha_Liman_Base" title="Pasha Liman Base">Albania</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-LarrabeeLesser94_259-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LarrabeeLesser94-259">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Iraq%E2%80%93Turkey_relations#Turkish_military_presence_in_Iraq" title="Iraq–Turkey relations">Iraq</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Qatar%E2%80%93Turkey_relations#Turkish_military_presence_in_Qatar" title="Qatar–Turkey relations">Qatar</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Camp_TURKSOM" title="Camp TURKSOM">Somalia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup> The country also maintains a force of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_military_forces_in_Northern_Cyprus" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish military forces in Northern Cyprus">36,000 troops</a> in <a href="/wiki/Northern_Cyprus" title="Northern Cyprus">Northern Cyprus</a> since 1974.<sup id="cite_ref-Richmond1998_263-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Richmond1998-263">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Human_rights">Human rights</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Turkey" title="Human rights in Turkey">Human rights in Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/2016%E2%80%93present_purges_in_Turkey" title="2016–present purges in Turkey">2016–present purges in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg/220px-Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg/330px-Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg/440px-Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Feminist_protest_from_Turkey.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Feminist demonstration in Kadıköy, Istanbul, on 29 July 2017.</div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Turkey" title="Human rights in Turkey">human rights record of Turkey</a> has been the subject of much controversy and international condemnation. Between 1959 and 2011 the <a href="/wiki/European_Court_of_Human_Rights" title="European Court of Human Rights">European Court of Human Rights</a> made more than 2400 judgements against Turkey for human rights violations on issues such as <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_of_Kurdish_people_in_Turkey" title="Human rights of Kurdish people in Turkey">Kurdish rights</a>, <a href="/wiki/Women_in_Turkey" title="Women in Turkey">women's rights</a>, <a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Turkey" title="LGBT rights in Turkey">LGBT rights</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Media of Turkey">media freedom</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ETCHR1_264-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ETCHR1-264">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-AnnualETCHR_265-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AnnualETCHR-265">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup> Turkey's human rights record continues to be a significant obstacle to the country's <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Turkey_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Turkey to the European Union">membership of the EU</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the latter half of the 1970s, Turkey suffered from <a href="/wiki/Political_violence_in_Turkey_(1976%E2%80%931980)" title="Political violence in Turkey (1976–1980)">political violence</a> between <a href="/wiki/Far-left_politics" title="Far-left politics">far-left</a> and <a href="/wiki/Far-right_politics" title="Far-right politics">far-right</a> militant groups, which culminated in the <a href="/wiki/1980_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1980 Turkish coup d&#39;état">military coup of 1980</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Kurdistan_Workers%27_Party" title="Kurdistan Workers&#39; Party">Kurdistan Workers' Party</a> (PKK, designated a <a href="/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups" title="List of designated terrorist groups">terrorist organisation</a> by Turkey, the United States,<sup id="cite_ref-department-of-state-list_151-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-department-of-state-list-151">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a><sup id="cite_ref-european-council-list_152-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-european-council-list-152">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup>) was founded in 1978 by a group of Kurdish militants led by <a href="/wiki/Abdullah_%C3%96calan" title="Abdullah Öcalan">Abdullah Öcalan</a>, seeking the foundation of an independent Kurdish state based on <a href="/wiki/Socialist_state" title="Socialist state">Marxist-Leninist</a> ideology.<sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup> The initial reason given by the PKK for this was the oppression of Kurds in Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-269" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-269">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kurdish%E2%80%93Turkish_conflict_(1978%E2%80%93present)" title="Kurdish–Turkish conflict (1978–present)">A full-scale insurgency</a> began <a href="/wiki/1984_PKK_attacks" title="1984 PKK attacks">in 1984</a>, when the PKK announced a Kurdish uprising. With time the PKK modified its demands into equal rights for ethnic Kurds and provincial autonomy within Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-272" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-272">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-274" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-274">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> Since 1980, the Turkish parliament stripped its members of <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_immunity" title="Parliamentary immunity">immunity</a> from prosecution, including 44 deputies most of which from the pro-Kurdish parties.<sup id="cite_ref-275" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-275">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>On 20 May 2016, the Turkish parliament stripped almost a quarter of its members of <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_immunity" title="Parliamentary immunity">immunity</a> from prosecution, including 101 deputies from the pro-Kurdish <a href="/wiki/Peoples%27_Democratic_Party_(Turkey)" title="Peoples&#39; Democratic Party (Turkey)">HDP</a> and the main opposition <a href="/wiki/Republican_People%27s_Party" title="Republican People&#39;s Party">CHP</a> party.<sup id="cite_ref-276" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-276">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-european_court_277-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-european_court-277">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup> By 2020, under the pretext of responding to a failed coup attempt in 2016,<sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup> authorities had arrested or imprisoned more than 90,000 Turkish citizens.<sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> According to the <a href="/wiki/Committee_to_Protect_Journalists" title="Committee to Protect Journalists">Committee to Protect Journalists</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Justice_and_Development_Party_(Turkey)" title="Justice and Development Party (Turkey)">AKP</a> government has waged  crackdowns on <a href="/wiki/Media_freedom_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Media freedom in Turkey">media freedom</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-CPJ_281-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CPJ-281">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cpj.org1_282-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cpj.org1-282">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> Many <a href="/wiki/List_of_arrested_journalists_in_Turkey" title="List of arrested journalists in Turkey">journalists have been arrested</a> using charges of "terrorism" and "anti-state activities".<sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup> In 2020, the CPJ identified 18 jailed journalists in Turkey (including the editorial staff of <i><a href="/wiki/Cumhuriyet" title="Cumhuriyet">Cumhuriyet</a></i>, Turkey's oldest newspaper still in circulation).<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="LGBT_rights">LGBT rights</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Turkey" title="LGBT rights in Turkey">LGBT rights in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg/220px-Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg/330px-Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg/440px-Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="640" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Gay_pride_Istanbul_2013_-_Taksim_Square.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Pride" title="Istanbul Pride">Istanbul Pride</a> was organized in 2003 for the first time. Since 2015, parades in <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a> have been denied permission by the government.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_286-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Homosexual" class="mw-redirect" title="Homosexual">Homosexual</a> activity has been legal in Turkey since <a href="/wiki/Tanzimat#Reforms" title="Tanzimat">1858</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/LGBT" title="LGBT">LGBT</a> people have had the right to seek asylum in Turkey under the <a href="/wiki/Convention_Relating_to_the_Status_of_Refugees" title="Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees">Geneva Convention</a> since 1951.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup> However, LGBT people in Turkey face discrimination, harassment and even violence from their relatives, neighbors, etc.<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> The Turkish authorities have carried out many discriminatory practices.<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup> Despite these, LGBT acceptance in Turkey is growing. In a survey conducted by <a href="/wiki/Kadir_Has_University" title="Kadir Has University">Kadir Has University</a> in Istanbul in 2016, 33% of respondents said that LGBT people should have equal rights, which increased to 45% in 2020. Another survey by Kadir Has University in 2018 found that the proportion of people who would not want a homosexual neighbour decreased from 55% in 2018 to 47% in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup> A poll by <a href="/wiki/Ipsos" title="Ipsos">Ipsos</a> in 2015 found that 27% of the Turkish public was in favour of legalizing same-sex marriage and 19% supported <a href="/wiki/Civil_unions" class="mw-redirect" title="Civil unions">civil unions</a> instead.<sup id="cite_ref-Ipsos_2015_295-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ipsos_2015-295">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When the annual <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Pride" title="Istanbul Pride">Istanbul Pride</a> was inaugurated in 2003, Turkey became the first Muslim-majority country to hold a gay pride march.<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> Since 2015, all types of parades at <a href="/wiki/Taksim_Square" title="Taksim Square">Taksim Square</a> and <a href="/wiki/%C4%B0stiklal_Avenue" title="İstiklal Avenue">İstiklal Avenue</a> (where, in 2013, the <a href="/wiki/Gezi_Park_protests" title="Gezi Park protests">Gezi Park protests</a> took place) have been denied permission by the <a href="/wiki/Justice_and_Development_Party_(Turkey)" title="Justice and Development Party (Turkey)">AKP</a> government, citing security concerns, but hundreds of people have defied the ban each year.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_286-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> Critics have claimed that the bans were in fact <a href="/wiki/Political_Islam" title="Political Islam">ideological</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_286-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Turkey" title="Geography of Turkey">Geography of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Turkey" title="List of national parks of Turkey">List of national parks of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:282px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Turkey_topo.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Turkey_topo.jpg/280px-Turkey_topo.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="150" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Turkey_topo.jpg/420px-Turkey_topo.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Turkey_topo.jpg/560px-Turkey_topo.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1400" data-file-height="752" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Turkey_topo.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Topographic_map" title="Topographic map">Topographic map</a> of Turkey</div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is a <a href="/wiki/Transcontinental_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Transcontinental country">transcontinental country</a> bridging <a href="/wiki/Southeastern_Europe" class="mw-redirect" title="Southeastern Europe">Southeastern Europe</a> and <a href="/wiki/Western_Asia" title="Western Asia">Western Asia</a>. Asian Turkey, which includes 97 percent of the country's territory, is separated from <a href="/wiki/East_Thrace" title="East Thrace">European Turkey</a> by the <a href="/wiki/Bosphorus" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosphorus">Bosphorus</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Marmara" title="Sea of Marmara">Sea of Marmara</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Dardanelles" title="Dardanelles">Dardanelles</a>. European Turkey comprises only 3 percent of the country's territory.<sup id="cite_ref-turkeygeoth_297-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-turkeygeoth-297">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup> Turkey covers an area of 783,562 square kilometres (302,535 square miles),<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 square miles) is in Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,175 square miles) is in Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-USLC_TRGeo_299-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-USLC_TRGeo-299">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> The country is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south. Turkey also contains the Sea of Marmara in the northwest.<sup id="cite_ref-TRGeo_TRMinistryTourism_300-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TRGeo_TRMinistryTourism-300">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:229px;max-width:229px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:227px;max-width:227px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Pamukkale_30.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Pamukkale_30.jpg/225px-Pamukkale_30.jpg" decoding="async" width="225" height="123" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Pamukkale_30.jpg/338px-Pamukkale_30.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Pamukkale_30.jpg/450px-Pamukkale_30.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4881" data-file-height="2675" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Pamukkale" title="Pamukkale">Pamukkale</a></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:227px;max-width:227px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg/225px-View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg" decoding="async" width="225" height="148" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg/338px-View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg/450px-View_of_Cappadocia_edit.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1514" data-file-height="996" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Cappadocia" title="Cappadocia">Cappadocia</a></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:227px;max-width:227px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg/225px-Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="225" height="127" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg/338px-Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg/450px-Salda_G%C3%B6l%C3%BC_2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5344" data-file-height="3008" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Lake_Salda" title="Lake Salda">Lake Salda</a></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is divided into seven geographical regions: <a href="/wiki/Marmara_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Marmara Region, Turkey">Marmara</a>, <a href="/wiki/Aegean_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Aegean Region, Turkey">Aegean</a>, <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Black Sea Region, Turkey">Black Sea</a>, <a href="/wiki/Central_Anatolia_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Central Anatolia Region, Turkey">Central Anatolia</a>, <a href="/wiki/East_Anatolia_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="East Anatolia Region, Turkey">Eastern Anatolia</a>, <a href="/wiki/South_Eastern_Anatolia_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="South Eastern Anatolia Region, Turkey">Southeastern Anatolia</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea_Region,_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Mediterranean Sea Region, Turkey">Mediterranean</a>. The uneven north Anatolian terrain running along the Black Sea resembles a long, narrow belt. This region comprises approximately one-sixth of Turkey's total land area. As a general trend, the inland Anatolian plateau becomes increasingly rugged as it progresses eastward.<sup id="cite_ref-TRGeo_TRMinistryTourism_300-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TRGeo_TRMinistryTourism-300">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup>
<a href="/wiki/Pamukkale" title="Pamukkale">Pamukkale</a> terraces are made of <a href="/wiki/Travertine" title="Travertine">travertine</a>, a sedimentary rock deposited by mineral water from the <a href="/wiki/Hot_springs" class="mw-redirect" title="Hot springs">hot springs</a>. The area is famous for a carbonate mineral left by the flowing of thermal spring water.<sup id="cite_ref-readers_natural_301-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-readers_natural-301">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Unesco_302-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Unesco-302">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup> It is located in Turkey's Inner Aegean region, in the <a href="/wiki/B%C3%BCy%C3%BCk_Menderes_River" title="Büyük Menderes River">River Menderes</a> (<a href="/wiki/Meander#Origin_of_term" title="Meander">Meander</a>) valley, which has a temperate climate for most of the year. It was added as a <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Turkey" title="List of World Heritage Sites in Turkey">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a> in 1988 with <a href="/wiki/Hierapolis" title="Hierapolis">Hierapolis</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/East_Thrace" title="East Thrace">East Thrace</a>, the European portion of Turkey, is located at the easternmost edge the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a>. It forms the border between Turkey and its neighbours Greece and Bulgaria. The Asian part of the country mostly consists of the peninsula of <a href="/wiki/Anatolia" title="Anatolia">Anatolia</a>, which consists of a high central plateau with narrow coastal plains, between the <a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ro%C4%9Flu_Mountains" title="Köroğlu Mountains">Köroğlu</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pontic_Mountains" title="Pontic Mountains">Pontic</a> mountain ranges to the north and the <a href="/wiki/Taurus_Mountains" title="Taurus Mountains">Taurus Mountains</a> to the south.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Anatolia_Region" title="Eastern Anatolia Region">Eastern Anatolia Region</a> mostly corresponds to the western part of the <a href="/wiki/Armenian_Highlands" class="mw-redirect" title="Armenian Highlands">Armenian Highlands</a> (the <a href="/wiki/Plateau" title="Plateau">plateau</a> situated between the <a href="/wiki/Anatolian_Plateau" title="Anatolian Plateau">Anatolian Plateau</a> in the west and the <a href="/wiki/Lesser_Caucasus" title="Lesser Caucasus">Lesser Caucasus</a> in the north)<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup> and contains <a href="/wiki/Mount_Ararat" title="Mount Ararat">Mount Ararat</a>, Turkey's highest point at 5,137 metres (16,854 feet),<sup id="cite_ref-mararat_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mararat-304">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Lake_Van" title="Lake Van">Lake Van</a>, the largest lake in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-lvan_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lvan-305">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> Eastern Turkey has a mountainous landscape and is home to the sources of rivers such as the <a href="/wiki/Euphrates" title="Euphrates">Euphrates</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tigris" title="Tigris">Tigris</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aras_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Aras River">Aras</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Southeastern_Anatolia_Region" title="Southeastern Anatolia Region">Southeastern Anatolia Region</a> includes the northern plains of <a href="/wiki/Upper_Mesopotamia" title="Upper Mesopotamia">Upper Mesopotamia</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Lakes_Region" title="Turkish Lakes Region">Lakes Region</a> (Turkish: <i>Göller Yöresi</i>) contains some of the largest lakes in Turkey, such as <a href="/wiki/Lake_Bey%C5%9Fehir" title="Lake Beyşehir">Lake Beyşehir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_E%C4%9Firdir" title="Lake Eğirdir">Lake Eğirdir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Burdur" title="Lake Burdur">Lake Burdur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Ak%C5%9Fehir" title="Lake Akşehir">Lake Akşehir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Eber" title="Lake Eber">Lake Eber</a> and <a href="/wiki/Lake_I%C5%9F%C4%B1kl%C4%B1" title="Lake Işıklı">Lake Işıklı</a>. <a href="/wiki/Lake_Tuz" title="Lake Tuz">Lake Tuz</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Nemrut" title="Lake Nemrut">Lake Nemrut</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_%C3%87%C4%B1ld%C4%B1r" title="Lake Çıldır">Lake Çıldır</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_%C4%B0znik" title="Lake İznik">Lake İznik</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Uluabat" title="Lake Uluabat">Lake Uluabat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Manyas" class="mw-redirect" title="Lake Manyas">Lake Manyas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Sapanca" title="Lake Sapanca">Lake Sapanca</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Salda" title="Lake Salda">Lake Salda</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lake_Meke" title="Lake Meke">Lake Meke</a> and <a href="/wiki/Uzung%C3%B6l" title="Uzungöl">Lake Uzungöl</a> are among other renowned lakes in Turkey. The rocks along the shoreline of Lake Salda were formed over time by microbes that trap minerals and sediments in the water.<sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda_306-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda-2_307-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-2-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> These so-called <a href="/wiki/Microbialite" title="Microbialite">microbialites</a> were once a major form of life on Earth and provide some of the oldest known fossilized records of life on our planet.<sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda_306-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda-2_307-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-2-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/NASA" title="NASA">NASA</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Mars_2020" title="Mars 2020">Mars 2020</a> mission <a href="/wiki/Perseverance_(rover)" title="Perseverance (rover)">Perseverance</a> <a href="/wiki/Mars_rover" title="Mars rover">rover</a> searches for signs of ancient life on the surface of <a href="/wiki/Mars" title="Mars">Mars</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda_306-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda-2_307-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-2-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> Studying these microbial fossils from Lake Salda has helped scientists prepare for the mission.<sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda_306-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NASA-Salda-2_307-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NASA-Salda-2-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> In March 2021, NASA reported that its Mars surface-exploring rover Perseverance showed that "the minerals and rock deposits at Lake Salda are the nearest match on Earth to those around the <a href="/wiki/Jezero_(crater)" title="Jezero (crater)">Jezero Crater</a> where the spacecraft landed."<sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Far from the coast the <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Turkey" title="Climate of Turkey">climate of Turkey</a> tends to be <a href="/wiki/Continental_climate" title="Continental climate">continental</a> but elsewhere <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate</a>, and has <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Turkey" title="Climate change in Turkey">become hotter</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Malatya_Plain" title="Malatya Plain">drier in parts</a>. There are <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_of_Turkey" title="Wildlife of Turkey">many species of plants and animals</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_of_Turkey" title="Wildlife of Turkey">Wildlife of Turkey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Turkey" title="Fauna of Turkey">Fauna of Turkey</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Flora_and_vegetation_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Flora and vegetation of Turkey">Flora and vegetation of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Turkey" title="Environmental issues in Turkey">Environmental issues in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG/220px-Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG/330px-Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG/440px-Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG 2x" data-file-width="3456" data-file-height="2592" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Sumela_Showing_Location.JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Sumela_Monastery" title="Sumela Monastery">Sumela Monastery</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Pontic_Mountains" title="Pontic Mountains">Pontic Mountains</a>, which form an <a href="/wiki/Ecoregion" title="Ecoregion">ecoregion</a> with <a href="/wiki/Northern_Anatolian_conifer_and_deciduous_forests" title="Northern Anatolian conifer and deciduous forests">diverse temperate rainforest types</a>, <a href="/wiki/Flora" title="Flora">flora</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fauna" title="Fauna">fauna</a> in northern Anatolia.</div></div></div>
<p>Turkey's extraordinary <a href="/wiki/Ecosystem" title="Ecosystem">ecosystem</a> and habitat diversity has produced considerable species diversity.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> Anatolia is the homeland of many plants that have been cultivated for food since the advent of <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, and the wild ancestors of many plants that now provide staples for humankind still grow in Turkey. The diversity of <a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Turkey" title="Fauna of Turkey">Turkey's fauna</a> is even greater than that of <a href="/wiki/Flora_and_vegetation_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Flora and vegetation of Turkey">its flora</a>. The number of animal species in the whole of Europe is around 60,000, while in Turkey there are over 80,000 (over 100,000 counting the subspecies).<sup id="cite_ref-allaboutturkey_310-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-allaboutturkey-310">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Northern_Anatolian_conifer_and_deciduous_forests" title="Northern Anatolian conifer and deciduous forests">Northern Anatolian conifer and deciduous forests</a> is an <a href="/wiki/Ecoregion" title="Ecoregion">ecoregion</a> which covers most of the <a href="/wiki/Pontic_Mountains" title="Pontic Mountains">Pontic Mountains</a> in northern Turkey, while the <a href="/wiki/Caucasus_mixed_forests" title="Caucasus mixed forests">Caucasus mixed forests</a> extend across the eastern end of the range. The region is home to <a href="/wiki/Eurasia" title="Eurasia">Eurasian</a> wildlife such as the <a href="/wiki/Eurasian_sparrowhawk" title="Eurasian sparrowhawk">Eurasian sparrowhawk</a>, <a href="/wiki/Golden_eagle" title="Golden eagle">golden eagle</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eastern_imperial_eagle" title="Eastern imperial eagle">eastern imperial eagle</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lesser_spotted_eagle" title="Lesser spotted eagle">lesser spotted eagle</a>, <a href="/wiki/Caucasian_black_grouse" class="mw-redirect" title="Caucasian black grouse">Caucasian black grouse</a>, <a href="/wiki/Red-fronted_serin" title="Red-fronted serin">red-fronted serin</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Wallcreeper" title="Wallcreeper">wallcreeper</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> The narrow coastal strip between the Pontic Mountains and the Black Sea is home to the <a href="/wiki/Euxine-Colchic_deciduous_forests" class="mw-redirect" title="Euxine-Colchic deciduous forests">Euxine-Colchic deciduous forests</a>, which contain some of the world's few <a href="/wiki/Temperate_rainforest" title="Temperate rainforest">temperate rainforests</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Pinus_brutia" title="Pinus brutia">Turkish pine (<i>Pinus brutia</i>)</a> is mostly found in Turkey and other east Mediterranean countries; the other commonly found species of the genus <a href="/wiki/Pine" title="Pine"><i>Pinus</i> (pine)</a> in Turkey include the <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_nigra" title="Pinus nigra">nigra</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_sylvestris" title="Pinus sylvestris">sylvestris</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_pinea" class="mw-redirect" title="Pinus pinea">pinea</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_halepensis" title="Pinus halepensis">halepensis</a></i>. The <a href="/wiki/Quercus_cerris" title="Quercus cerris">Turkey oak (<i>Quercus cerris</i>)</a> and numerous other species of the genus <a href="/wiki/Oak" title="Oak"><i>Quercus</i> (oak)</a> exist in Turkey. The most commonly found species of the genus <a href="/wiki/Platanus" title="Platanus"><i>Platanus</i> (plane)</a> is the <i><a href="/wiki/Platanus_orientalis" title="Platanus orientalis">orientalis</a></i>. Several wild species of <a href="/wiki/Tulip" title="Tulip">tulip</a> are native to Anatolia, and the flower was first <a href="/wiki/Tulip#Introduction_to_Western_Europe" title="Tulip">introduced to Western Europe</a> with species taken from the Ottoman Empire in the 16th century.<sup id="cite_ref-Blunt_7_313-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Blunt_7-313">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:202px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg/200px-Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="200" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg/300px-Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg/400px-Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="600" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Odd-eyed_Turkish_Angora_cat_-_20080830.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A white <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Angora" title="Turkish Angora">Turkish Angora</a> cat with <a href="/wiki/Odd-eyed_cat" title="Odd-eyed cat">odd eyes (heterochromia)</a>, which is common among the Angoras.</div></div></div>
<p>There are <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Turkey" title="List of national parks of Turkey">40 national parks</a>, 189 nature parks, 31 nature preserve areas, 80 wildlife protection areas and 109 nature monuments in Turkey such as <a href="/wiki/Gallipoli_Peninsula_Historical_National_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Gallipoli Peninsula Historical National Park">Gallipoli Peninsula Historical National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mount_Nemrut_National_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Mount Nemrut National Park">Mount Nemrut National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Troy" title="Troy">Ancient Troy National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C3%96l%C3%BCdeniz_Nature_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Ölüdeniz Nature Park">Ölüdeniz Nature Park</a> and <a href="/wiki/Polonezk%C3%B6y_Nature_Park" title="Polonezköy Nature Park">Polonezköy Nature Park</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ministryofforest_315-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministryofforest-315">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> In the 21st century, threats to biodiversity include <a href="/wiki/Desertification" title="Desertification">desertification</a> due to <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Turkey" title="Climate change in Turkey">climate change in Turkey</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Anatolian_leopard" class="mw-redirect" title="Anatolian leopard">Anatolian leopard</a> is still found in very small numbers in the northeastern and southeastern regions of Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-O.E.Can_317-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-O.E.Can-317">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Eurasian_lynx" title="Eurasian lynx">Eurasian lynx</a>, the <a href="/wiki/European_wildcat" title="European wildcat">European wildcat</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Caracal" title="Caracal">Caracal</a> are other <a href="/wiki/Felidae" title="Felidae">felid</a> species which are currently found in the forests of Turkey. The <a href="/wiki/Caspian_tiger" title="Caspian tiger">Caspian tiger</a>, now extinct, lived in the easternmost regions of Turkey until the latter half of the 20th century.<sup id="cite_ref-O.E.Can_317-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-O.E.Can-317">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Üstay_319-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Üstay-319">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Renowned domestic animals from <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a>, the capital of Turkey, include the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Angora" title="Turkish Angora">Angora cat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Angora_rabbit" title="Angora rabbit">Angora rabbit</a> and <a href="/wiki/Angora_goat" title="Angora goat">Angora goat</a>; and from <a href="/wiki/Van_Province" title="Van Province">Van Province</a> the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Van" title="Turkish Van">Van cat</a>. The national dog breeds are the <a href="/wiki/Kangal_Shepherd_Dog" title="Kangal Shepherd Dog">Kangal</a> (<a href="/wiki/Anatolian_Shepherd" class="mw-redirect" title="Anatolian Shepherd">Anatolian Shepherd</a>), <a href="/wiki/Aksaray_Malaklisi" title="Aksaray Malaklisi">Malaklı</a> and <a href="/wiki/Akbash" title="Akbash">Akbaş</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-gateofturkey_320-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gateofturkey-320">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Turkey" title="Climate of Turkey">Climate of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Turkey" title="Climate change in Turkey">Climate change in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:302px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg/300px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="140" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg/450px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg/600px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1816" data-file-height="850" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Koppen-Geiger_Map_TUR_present.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification" title="Köppen climate classification">Köppen climate classification</a> of Turkey</div></div></div>
<p>The coastal areas of Turkey bordering the <a href="/wiki/Aegean_Sea" title="Aegean Sea">Aegean</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Seas</a> have a <a href="/wiki/Temperate" class="mw-redirect" title="Temperate">temperate</a> <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_climate" title="Mediterranean climate">Mediterranean climate</a>, with hot, dry summers and mild to cool, wet winters.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> The coastal areas bordering the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> have a temperate <a href="/wiki/Oceanic_climate" title="Oceanic climate">oceanic climate</a> with warm, wet summers and cool to cold, wet <a href="/wiki/Winter" title="Winter">winters</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> The Turkish Black Sea coast receives the most <a href="/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Precipitation (meteorology)">precipitation</a> and is the only region of Turkey that receives high precipitation throughout the year.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> The eastern part of the Black Sea coast averages 2,200 millimetres (87&#160;in) annually which is the highest precipitation in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> The coastal areas bordering the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Marmara" title="Sea of Marmara">Sea of Marmara</a>, which connects the Aegean Sea and the Black Sea, have a transitional climate between a temperate Mediterranean climate and a
