temperate oceanic climate with warm to hot, moderately dry <a href="/wiki/Summer" title="Summer">summers</a> and cool to cold, wet winters.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> Snow falls on the coastal areas of the Sea of Marmara and the Black Sea almost every winter, but usually melts in no more than a few days.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> However, snow is rare in the coastal areas of the Aegean Sea and very rare in the coastal areas of the Mediterranean Sea.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> Winters on the Anatolian plateau are especially severe. Temperatures of −30&#160;°C to −40&#160;°C (−22&#160;°F to −40&#160;°F) do occur in northeastern Anatolia, and snow may lie on the ground for at least 120 days of the year, and during the entire year on the summits of the highest mountains. In central Anatolia the temperatures can drop below −20&#160;°C ( -4&#160;°F) with the mountains being even colder.
</p><p>Mountains close to the coast prevent Mediterranean influences from extending inland, giving the central Anatolian <a href="/wiki/Plateau" title="Plateau">plateau</a> of the interior of Turkey a <a href="/wiki/Continental_climate" title="Continental climate">continental climate</a> with sharply contrasting <a href="/wiki/Seasons" class="mw-redirect" title="Seasons">seasons</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Meteo_321-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meteo-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Turkey" title="Economy of Turkey">Economy of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:302px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg/300px-Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="183" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg/450px-Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg/600px-Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5619" data-file-height="3421" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Levent_Financial_Center_-_Istanbul.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Akbank" title="Akbank">Akbank</a>, <a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrkiye_%C4%B0%C5%9F_Bankas%C4%B1" class="mw-redirect" title="Türkiye İş Bankası">Türkiye İş Bankası</a>, <a href="/wiki/Yap%C4%B1_Kredi" title="Yapı Kredi">Yapı Kredi</a>, <a href="/wiki/QNB_Finansbank" title="QNB Finansbank">QNB Finansbank</a> and <a href="/wiki/Garanti_BBVA" title="Garanti BBVA">Garanti BBVA</a> are among the Turkish banks headquartered in <a href="/wiki/Levent" title="Levent">Levent</a>, <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a>.</div></div></div>
<p>Turkey is a <a href="/wiki/Newly_industrialized_country" title="Newly industrialized country">newly industrialized country</a>, with an upper-middle income economy, which is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)" title="List of countries by GDP (nominal)">twentieth-largest in the world</a> by nominal GDP, and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(PPP)" title="List of countries by GDP (PPP)">eleventh-largest</a> by <a href="/wiki/Purchasing_power_parity" title="Purchasing power parity">PPP</a>. Turkey is one of the <a href="/wiki/Emerging_7" class="mw-redirect" title="Emerging 7">Emerging 7</a> countries. According to <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">IMF</a> estimates, Turkey's GDP per capita by PPP is $40,883 in 2023<sup id="cite_ref-IMF-WEO_9-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMF-WEO-9">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> and approximately 11.7% of Turks are at risk of poverty or social exclusion as of 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup> Unemployment in Turkey was 13.6% in 2019,<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> and the middle class population in Turkey rose from 18% to 41% of the population between 1993 and 2010 according to the World Bank.<sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of September&#160;2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Turkey&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, the foreign currency reserves of the <a href="/wiki/Central_Bank_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey" title="Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey">Turkish Central Bank</a> were $74.9 billion (an 8.1% increase compared to the previous month), its gold reserves were $38.5 billion (a 5.1% decrease compared to the previous month), while its official reserve assets stood at $121.3 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> As of October&#160;2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Turkey&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, the foreign currency deposits of the citizens and residents in <a href="/wiki/List_of_banks_in_Turkey" title="List of banks in Turkey">Turkish banks</a> stood at $234 billion, equivalent to around half of all deposits.<sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/European_Union_%E2%80%93_Turkey_Customs_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="European Union – Turkey Customs Union">EU–Turkey Customs Union</a> in 1995 led to an extensive liberalisation of tariff rates, and forms one of the most important pillars of Turkey's foreign trade policy.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Foreign_direct_investment" title="Foreign direct investment">Foreign direct investment</a> (FDI) in Turkey reached 22.05 billion USD in 2007 and 19.26 billion USD in 2015, but has declined in recent years.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg/170px-2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="224" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg/255px-2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg/340px-2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3024" data-file-height="3985" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:2022_Togg_C-SUV.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Togg_C-SUV" title="Togg C-SUV">Togg C-SUV</a><sup id="cite_ref-insideevs_330-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-insideevs-330">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup> produced by <a href="/wiki/Togg" title="Togg">Togg</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup> a <a href="/wiki/Automotive_industry_in_Turkey" title="Automotive industry in Turkey">Turkish automotive company</a> established in 2018 for producing <a href="/wiki/Electric_vehicle" title="Electric vehicle">EVs</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Jay_Ramey_332-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jay_Ramey-332">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Togg-2022_333-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Togg-2022-333">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-insideevs_330-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-insideevs-330">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Automotive_industry_in_Turkey" title="Automotive industry in Turkey">automotive industry in Turkey</a> is sizeable, and produced 1,276,140 motor vehicles in 2021, ranking as the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_motor_vehicle_production" title="List of countries by motor vehicle production">13th largest producer in the world</a> (production peaked at 1,695,731 motor vehicles in 2017, when Turkey also <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_motor_vehicle_production" title="List of countries by motor vehicle production">ranked 13th</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> Turkish automotive companies like <a href="/wiki/TEMSA" title="TEMSA">TEMSA</a>, <a href="/wiki/Otokar" title="Otokar">Otokar</a> and <a href="/wiki/BMC_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="BMC (Turkey)">BMC</a> are among the world's largest van, bus and truck manufacturers. <a href="/wiki/Togg" title="Togg">Togg</a>, or Turkey's Automobile Joint Venture Group Inc., is the first all-electric vehicle company of Turkey. Turkish <a href="/wiki/Shipyard" title="Shipyard">shipyards</a> are highly regarded both for the production of chemical and <a href="/wiki/Oil_tanker" title="Oil tanker">oil tankers</a> up to 10,000 <a href="/wiki/Deadweight_tonnage" title="Deadweight tonnage">dwt</a> and also for their <a href="/wiki/Mega_yacht" class="mw-redirect" title="Mega yacht">mega yachts</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ship-oecd_335-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ship-oecd-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> Turkish brands like <a href="/wiki/Beko" title="Beko">Beko</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vestel" title="Vestel">Vestel</a> are among the largest producers of <a href="/wiki/Consumer_electronics" title="Consumer electronics">consumer electronics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Home_appliances" class="mw-redirect" title="Home appliances">home appliances</a> in Europe, and invest a substantial amount of funds for research and development in new technologies related to these fields.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Other key sectors of the Turkish economy are <a href="/wiki/List_of_banks_in_Turkey" title="List of banks in Turkey">banking</a>, construction, home appliances, electronics, textiles, oil refining, petrochemical products, food, mining, iron and steel, and <a href="/wiki/Machine_industry" title="Machine industry">machine industry</a>. According to a Turkish Statistical Institute survey in 2021, which used the available data for 2020, it was estimated that 46.7 percent of total disposable income was received by the top 20 percent of income earners, while the lowest 20 percent received only 6.1 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2020 the <a href="/wiki/International_Energy_Agency" title="International Energy Agency">International Energy Agency</a> stated that <a href="/wiki/Energy_subsidy#Turkey" title="Energy subsidy">fossil fuel subsidies</a> should be redirected, for example to the <a href="/wiki/Health_in_Turkey" title="Health in Turkey">healthcare system</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> Fossil fuel subsidies were around 0.2% of the GDP during the first two decades of the 21st century,<sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_342-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> and are higher than clean <a href="/wiki/Energy_subsidies" class="mw-redirect" title="Energy subsidies">energy subsidies</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/External_cost" class="mw-redirect" title="External cost">external cost</a> of fossil fuel consumption in 2018 has been estimated as 1.5% of GDP.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> In 2020 the <a href="/wiki/European_Bank_for_Reconstruction_and_Development" title="European Bank for Reconstruction and Development">European Bank for Reconstruction and Development</a> offered to support a <a href="/wiki/Just_transition" title="Just transition">just transition</a> away from coal.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_345-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> Increasing the share of renewable energy could reduce inflation.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of 2023, two Turkish tech startups, <a href="/wiki/Getir" title="Getir">Getir</a> and <a href="/wiki/Trendyol" title="Trendyol">Trendyol</a>, have market valuations above $10 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> Turkey has seen a growth in the <a href="/wiki/Video_gaming_industry" class="mw-redirect" title="Video gaming industry">video gaming industry</a> in recent years. Numerous game developing companies have been established and gained investment from venture capitalists.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/TaleWorlds_Entertainment" title="TaleWorlds Entertainment">TaleWorlds Entertainment</a>, <a href="/wiki/Peak_Games" title="Peak Games">Peak Games</a>, Bigger Games and Dream Games are the current leaders in this sector.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tourism">Tourism</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Turkey" title="Tourism in Turkey">Tourism in Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Turkey" title="List of World Heritage Sites in Turkey">List of World Heritage Sites in Turkey</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tentative_list_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Turkey" title="Tentative list of World Heritage Sites in Turkey">Tentative list of World Heritage Sites in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:312px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Marmaris_harbor_(aerial_view),_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province,_southwest_Turkey,_Mediterranean.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg/310px-Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg" decoding="async" width="310" height="135" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg/465px-Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg/620px-Marmaris_harbor_%28aerial_view%29%2C_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province%2C_southwest_Turkey%2C_Mediterranean.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="1738" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Marmaris_harbor_(aerial_view),_Mu%C4%9Fla_Province,_southwest_Turkey,_Mediterranean.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Marmaris" title="Marmaris">Marmaris</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Riviera" title="Turkish Riviera">Turkish Riviera</a></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Turkey" title="Tourism in Turkey">Tourism in Turkey</a> has increased almost every year in the 21st century,<sup id="cite_ref-TourismStats2018_352-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TourismStats2018-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> and is an important part of the economy. The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Ministry_of_Culture_and_Tourism" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism">Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism</a> currently promotes Turkish tourism under the project <a href="/wiki/Turkey_Home" title="Turkey Home">Turkey Home</a>. Turkey is one of the world's top ten destination countries, with the highest percentage of foreign visitors arriving from Europe; specially Germany and Russia in recent years.<sup id="cite_ref-TourismStats2018_352-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TourismStats2018-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> In 2019, Turkey <a href="/wiki/World_Tourism_rankings#Most_visited_destinations_by_international_tourist_arrivals" title="World Tourism rankings">ranked sixth in the world</a> in terms of the number of international tourist arrivals behind <a href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italy</a>, with 51.2 million foreign tourists visiting the country.<sup id="cite_ref-WTO_Tourism_Highlights_2019_Edition_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WTO_Tourism_Highlights_2019_Edition-353">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup> Turkey has <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Turkey" title="List of World Heritage Sites in Turkey">19 UNESCO World Heritage Sites</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Turkey_(Tentative_list)" class="mw-redirect" title="List of World Heritage Sites in Turkey (Tentative list)">84 World Heritage Sites in tentative list</a>. Turkey is home to 519 <a href="/wiki/Blue_Flag_beaches" class="mw-redirect" title="Blue Flag beaches">Blue Flag beaches</a>, which makes it in the third place in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a> is the tenth most visited city in the world with 13,433,000 annual visitors as of 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Antalya" title="Antalya">Antalya</a> is the second most visited city in Turkey, with over 9 million tourists in 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Infrastructure">Infrastructure</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Transport_in_Turkey" title="Transport in Turkey">Transport in Turkey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Communications_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Communications in Turkey">Communications in Turkey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Energy_in_Turkey" title="Energy in Turkey">Energy in Turkey</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Water_supply_and_sanitation_in_Turkey" title="Water supply and sanitation in Turkey">Water supply and sanitation in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:312px;"><a href="/wiki/File:%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg/310px-%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg" decoding="async" width="310" height="207" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg/465px-%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg/620px-%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4808" data-file-height="3205" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:%C4%B0stanbul_Havaliman%C4%B1_Airport_2019_24.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The main terminal of <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Airport" title="Istanbul Airport">Istanbul Airport</a> has an annual passenger capacity of 90 million and is the <a href="/wiki/Airport_terminal#Records" title="Airport terminal">world's largest terminal building under a single roof</a>. It is the hub of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Airlines" title="Turkish Airlines">Turkish Airlines</a>, which serves more destinations than any other airline in the world<sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> and flies to 126 countries, <a href="/wiki/World%27s_largest_airlines#By_number_of_countries_served" class="mw-redirect" title="World&#39;s largest airlines">more than any other airline</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_286-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:4_358-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-dests_359-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dests-359">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>In 2013 there were 98 <a href="/wiki/List_of_airports_in_Turkey" title="List of airports in Turkey">airports in Turkey</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> including 22 <a href="/wiki/International_airport" title="International airport">international airports</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Airport" title="Istanbul Airport">Istanbul Airport</a> is planned to be the largest airport in the world, with a capacity to serve 150 million passengers a year.<sup id="cite_ref-dhmi_363-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhmi-363">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Airlines" title="Turkish Airlines">Turkish Airlines</a> uses the Istanbul Airport, which has a current annual capacity of serving 90 million passengers, as its main hub. As well as Turkish Airlines, the <a href="/wiki/Flag_carrier" title="Flag carrier">flag carrier</a> of Turkey since 1933, <a href="/wiki/List_of_airlines_of_Turkey" title="List of airlines of Turkey">several other airlines operate in the country</a>. Turkish Airlines has scheduled services to 315 destinations in <a href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Americas" title="Americas">Americas</a>, making it the <a href="/wiki/Largest_airlines_in_the_world" title="Largest airlines in the world">largest</a> <a href="/wiki/Mainline_(aeronautics)" title="Mainline (aeronautics)">mainline carrier</a> in the world <a href="/wiki/Largest_airlines_in_the_world#By_number_of_countries_served" title="Largest airlines in the world">by number of countries served</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-air_profit_366-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-air_profit-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:4_358-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of 2014<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Turkey&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, the country has a roadway network of over 65,000 kilometres (40,400 miles).<sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> Motorways are controlled-access highways that are officially named <a href="/wiki/Otoyol" title="Otoyol">Otoyol</a>. The network spans 3,523 kilometres (2,189&#160;mi) as of 2020. The network is expected to expand to 4,773 kilometres (2,966&#160;mi) by 2023 and to 9,312 kilometres (5,786&#160;mi) by 2035.<sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Opened in 2013, the <a href="/wiki/Marmaray" title="Marmaray">Marmaray tunnel</a> under the <a href="/wiki/Bosphorus" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosphorus">Bosphorus</a> connects the railway and <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Metro" title="Istanbul Metro">metro</a> lines of Istanbul's European and Asian sides; while the nearby <a href="/wiki/Eurasia_Tunnel" title="Eurasia Tunnel">Eurasia Tunnel</a> (2016) provides an undersea road connection for motor vehicles.<sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Metro" title="Istanbul Metro">Istanbul Metro</a> is the largest metro network in the country with 495 million annual ridership.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup> There are 9 metro lines under service and 6 more under construction.<sup id="cite_ref-network_371-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-network-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg/220px-1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="158" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg/330px-1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg/440px-1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3702" data-file-height="2665" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge_20220327.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge" title="1915 Çanakkale Bridge">1915 Çanakkale Bridge</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Dardanelles" title="Dardanelles">Dardanelles</a> strait, connecting Europe and Asia, is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_longest_suspension_bridge_spans#Completed_suspension_bridges" title="List of longest suspension bridge spans">longest suspension bridge in the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-B1M_372-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-B1M-372">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-hdn_373-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hdn-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Bosphorus_Bridge" title="Bosphorus Bridge">Bosphorus Bridge</a> (1973), <a href="/wiki/Fatih_Sultan_Mehmet_Bridge" title="Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge">Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge</a> (1988) and <a href="/wiki/Yavuz_Sultan_Selim_Bridge" title="Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge">Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge</a> (2016) are the three suspension bridges connecting the European and Asian shores of the <a href="/wiki/Bosphorus" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosphorus">Bosphorus</a> strait in Istanbul.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/%C3%87anakkale_1915_Bridge" class="mw-redirect" title="Çanakkale 1915 Bridge">Çanakkale 1915 Bridge</a> (2022) on the <a href="/wiki/Dardanelles" title="Dardanelles">Dardanelles</a> strait, connecting Europe and Asia, is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_longest_suspension_bridge_spans#Bridges_under_construction" title="List of longest suspension bridge spans">longest suspension bridge in the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-B1M_372-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-B1M-372">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-hdn_373-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hdn-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Osman_Gazi_Bridge" title="Osman Gazi Bridge">Osman Gazi Bridge</a> (2016) connects the northern and southern shores of the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_%C4%B0zmit" title="Gulf of İzmit">Gulf of İzmit</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Turkish_State_Railways" title="Turkish State Railways">Turkish State Railways</a> operates both conventional and high speed trains on 12,532 kilometres rail length. The government-owned national railway company started building <a href="/wiki/High-speed_rail_in_Turkey" title="High-speed rail in Turkey">high-speed rail</a> lines in 2003. The <a href="/wiki/Ankara-Konya_high-speed_railway" class="mw-redirect" title="Ankara-Konya high-speed railway">Ankara-Konya line</a> became operational in 2011, while the <a href="/wiki/Ankara-Istanbul_high-speed_railway" class="mw-redirect" title="Ankara-Istanbul high-speed railway">Ankara-Istanbul line</a> entered service in 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-hizlitren.tcdd.gov.tr_374-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hizlitren.tcdd.gov.tr-374">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> Konya-Karaman line started its operations in 2022 and 406&#160;km (252&#160;mi) long <a href="/wiki/Ankara%E2%80%93Sivas_high-speed_railway" title="Ankara–Sivas high-speed railway">Ankara-Sivas line</a> is to open in 2022.  
</p><p>As of 2018<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Turkey&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup> Turkey consumes 1700 <a href="/wiki/Terawatt" class="mw-redirect" title="Terawatt">terawatt</a> hours (TW/h) of <a href="/wiki/Primary_energy" title="Primary energy">primary energy</a> per year, a little over 20 <a href="/wiki/Megawatt" class="mw-redirect" title="Megawatt">megawatt</a> hours (MW/h) per person, mostly from imported <a href="/wiki/Fossil_fuels" class="mw-redirect" title="Fossil fuels">fossil fuels</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> Although the <a href="/wiki/Energy_policy_of_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Energy policy of Turkey">energy policy of Turkey</a> includes reducing fossil-fuel imports, <a href="/wiki/Coal_in_Turkey" title="Coal in Turkey">coal in Turkey</a> is the largest single reason why <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions_by_Turkey" title="Greenhouse gas emissions by Turkey">greenhouse gas emissions by Turkey</a> amount to 1% of the global total. <a href="/wiki/Renewable_energy_in_Turkey" title="Renewable energy in Turkey">Renewable energy in Turkey</a> is being increased and the <a href="/wiki/Akkuyu_Nuclear_Power_Plant" title="Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant">Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant</a> is being built on the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean</a> coast. However, despite the overcapacity in <a href="/wiki/Electricity_sector_in_Turkey" title="Electricity sector in Turkey">national electricity generation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fossil_fuel_subsidies" title="Fossil fuel subsidies">fossil fuels are still subsidized</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019 Turkey had the <a href="/wiki/Geothermal_power#Utility-grade_stations" title="Geothermal power">fourth-highest direct utilisation and capacity</a> of <a href="/wiki/Geothermal_power_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Geothermal power in Turkey">geothermal power</a> in the world,<sup id="cite_ref-2019_Capacity_377-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2019_Capacity-377">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> and produced 45.6% of its electricity from renewable sources.<sup id="cite_ref-ieaTurkey_378-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ieaTurkey-378">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_State_Railways" title="Turkish State Railways">Turkish State Railways</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Ankara_Tren_Gar%C4%B1" title="Ankara Tren Garı">ATG terminal</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a></div></div></div></div>
<p>Many <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Natural gas in Turkey">natural gas</a> pipelines span the country's territory.<sup id="cite_ref-CIAFactbookTurkey_172-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CIAFactbookTurkey-172">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Blue_Stream" title="Blue Stream">Blue Stream</a>, a major trans-<a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> gas pipeline, delivers natural gas from Russia to Turkey as does the undersea pipeline, <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Stream" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Stream">Turkish Stream</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan_pipeline" class="mw-redirect" title="Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline">Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline</a>, the second longest <a href="/wiki/Oil_pipeline" class="mw-redirect" title="Oil pipeline">oil pipeline</a> in the world, was inaugurated in 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-emreozgur.com_380-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-emreozgur.com-380">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of 2022, almost all natural gas consumed in Turkey is imported, but production from the <a href="/wiki/Sakarya_Gas_Field" class="mw-redirect" title="Sakarya Gas Field">Sakarya Gas Field</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Sweet_gas" class="mw-redirect" title="Sweet gas">sweet gas</a> field in the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> discovered by <a href="/wiki/TPAO" title="TPAO">TPAO</a> in 2020,<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup> is due to start in 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> TPAO estimates reserves over 500 bcm.<sup id="cite_ref-383" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-383">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup> A pipeline will connect the gas field to the <a href="/wiki/Filyos_Natural-gas_Processing_Plant" title="Filyos Natural-gas Processing Plant">Filyos Natural-gas Processing Plant</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup> and TPAO plans to begin production in 2023,<sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> with an estimated peak production of 40 bcm in 2026.<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup> By the end of December 2022, the total volume of natural gas Turkey has discovered in the Black Sea amounted to 710 billion cubic metres (bcm) after a new field was located and a previous find was revised higher.<sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Science_and_technology">Science and technology</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Turkey" title="Science and technology in Turkey">Science and technology in Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:252px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg/250px-Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg/375px-Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg/500px-Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2268" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Library_Main_Hall_Columns.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Presidential_Library_(Turkey)" title="Presidential Library (Turkey)">Presidential Library</a> in <a href="/wiki/Ankara" title="Ankara">Ankara</a> is the largest library in Turkey, with a collection of over 4 million printed books<sup id="cite_ref-Presidential_Library_388-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Presidential_Library-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup> and over 120 million electronic editions<sup id="cite_ref-Presidential_Library_388-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Presidential_Library-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup> published in 134 languages.<sup id="cite_ref-Presidential_Library_388-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Presidential_Library-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Scientific_and_Technological_Research_Council_of_Turkey" title="Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey">TÜBİTAK</a> is the leading agency for developing <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Turkey" title="Science and technology in Turkey">science, technology and innovation policies in Turkey</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Academy_of_Sciences" title="Turkish Academy of Sciences">TÜBA</a> is an autonomous scholarly society acting to promote scientific activities in Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/TAEK" class="mw-redirect" title="TAEK">TAEK</a> is the country's official <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_technology" title="Nuclear technology">nuclear energy</a> institution, focused on academic research and the development and implementation of peaceful nuclear technology.<sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> It is supervising the construction of Turkey's first nuclear facility, <a href="/wiki/Akkuyu_Nuclear_Power_Plant" title="Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant">Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant</a> in <a href="/wiki/Mersin" title="Mersin">Mersin</a>, at the cost of $20 billion; the plant is expected to be operational in May 2023,<sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup> and is projected to meet around 10% of the country's electricity demand.
</p><p>The Turkish government invests heavily in <a href="/wiki/Research_and_development" title="Research and development">research and development</a> of <a href="/wiki/Military_technology" title="Military technology">military technologies</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Aerospace_Industries" title="Turkish Aerospace Industries">Turkish Aerospace Industries</a>, <a href="/wiki/Aselsan" title="Aselsan">Aselsan</a>, <a href="/wiki/HAVELSAN" title="HAVELSAN">HAVELSAN</a>, <a href="/wiki/Roketsan" title="Roketsan">Roketsan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mechanical_and_Chemical_Industry_Corporation" title="Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation">MKE</a>. Turkey is a global leader in <a href="/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle" title="Unmanned aerial vehicle">unmanned aerial vehicles</a> (UAV); the <a href="/wiki/Baykar_Bayraktar_TB2" title="Baykar Bayraktar TB2">Bayraktar TB2</a>, manufactured by private defence company <a href="/wiki/Baykar" title="Baykar">Baykar</a>, has been exported to over a dozen countries and played a decisive role in several conflicts, including the <a href="/wiki/2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_war" class="mw-redirect" title="2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war">2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war</a> and the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-393" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-393">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Turkey has made significant inroads in aerospace technology into the 21st century. In 2013, it initiated the <a href="/wiki/Space_Launch_System_(Turkey)" title="Space Launch System (Turkey)">Turkish Space Launch System</a> (UFS) to develop an independent satellite launch capability<sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-MSLS_396-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MSLS-396">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Roketsan_Şimşek_397-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roketsan_Şimşek-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> up to an <a href="/wiki/Low_Earth_orbit#Examples" title="Low Earth orbit">altitude of 550&#160;km (342&#160;mi)</a><sup id="cite_ref-Roketsan_Şimşek_397-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roketsan_Şimşek-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> with the <a href="/wiki/Roketsan" title="Roketsan">Roketsan</a> Şimşek-1 rocket by 2027,<sup id="cite_ref-Roketsan_Şimşek_397-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roketsan_Şimşek-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> and the longer range Şimşek-2 by 2028,<sup id="cite_ref-Roketsan_Şimşek_397-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roketsan_Şimşek-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> including the construction of a <a href="/wiki/Spaceport" title="Spaceport">spaceport</a>, the development of <a href="/wiki/Satellite_launch_vehicle" class="mw-redirect" title="Satellite launch vehicle">satellite launch vehicles</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-MSLS_396-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MSLS-396">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Roketsan_Şimşek_397-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roketsan_Şimşek-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> and the establishment of remote Earth stations.<sup id="cite_ref-ssm1_398-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ssm1-398">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-dn1_399-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dn1-399">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-dn2_400-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dn2-400">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup> 
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:TaiIDEF2015_(8).JPG" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG/220px-TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG/330px-TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG/440px-TaiIDEF2015_%288%29.JPG 2x" data-file-width="3696" data-file-height="2448" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:TaiIDEF2015_(8).JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/G%C3%B6kt%C3%BCrk-1" title="Göktürk-1">Göktürk-1</a>, <a href="/wiki/G%C3%B6kt%C3%BCrk-2" title="Göktürk-2">Göktürk-2</a> and <a href="/wiki/G%C3%B6kt%C3%BCrk-3" title="Göktürk-3">Göktürk-3</a> are the <a href="/wiki/Earth_observation_satellite" title="Earth observation satellite">Earth observation satellites</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_National_Defense_(Turkey)" title="Ministry of National Defense (Turkey)">Turkish Ministry of National Defense</a>, while state-owned <a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrksat_(company)" title="Türksat (company)">Türksat</a> operates the <a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrksat_(satellite)" title="Türksat (satellite)">Türksat series</a> of <a href="/wiki/Communications_satellite" title="Communications satellite">communications satellites</a>.</div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrksat_(company)" title="Türksat (company)">Türksat</a>, the country's sole <a href="/wiki/Communications_satellite" title="Communications satellite">communications satellite</a> operator, has launched a <a href="/wiki/Turksat_(satellite)" class="mw-redirect" title="Turksat (satellite)">series of satellites</a> into orbit; likewise, the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Satellite_Assembly,_Integration_and_Test_Center" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Satellite Assembly, Integration and Test Center">Turkish Satellite Assembly, Integration and Test Center</a> (UMET)—a spacecraft production and testing facility owned by the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_National_Defence_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of National Defence (Turkey)">Ministry of National Defence</a> and operated by the TAI—has launched the <a href="/wiki/G%C3%B6kt%C3%BCrk-1" title="Göktürk-1">Göktürk series</a> of <a href="/wiki/Earth_observation_satellite" title="Earth observation satellite">Earth observation satellites</a> for <a href="/wiki/Reconnaissance" title="Reconnaissance">reconnaissance</a>; <a href="/wiki/BILSAT-1" title="BILSAT-1">BILSAT-1</a> and <a href="/wiki/RASAT" title="RASAT">RASAT</a> are the scientific Earth observation satellites operated by the <a href="/wiki/T%C3%9CB%C4%B0TAK_Space_Technologies_Research_Institute" title="TÜBİTAK Space Technologies Research Institute">TÜBİTAK Space Technologies Research Institute</a>.
</p><p>In 2015, <a href="/wiki/Aziz_Sancar" title="Aziz Sancar">Aziz Sancar</a>, a Turkish professor at the <a href="/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina" title="University of North Carolina">University of North Carolina</a>, won the <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Chemistry_Prize" class="mw-redirect" title="Nobel Chemistry Prize">Nobel Prize in Chemistry</a> for his work on how cells repair damaged DNA;<sup id="cite_ref-401" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-401">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup> he is one of <a href="/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_by_country#Turkey" title="List of Nobel laureates by country">two Turkish Nobel laureates</a>, and the first in the sciences. Other prominent Turkish scientists include physician <a href="/wiki/Hulusi_Beh%C3%A7et" title="Hulusi Behçet">Hulusi Behçet</a>, who discovered <a href="/wiki/Beh%C3%A7et%27s_disease" title="Behçet&#39;s disease">Behçet's disease</a>; mathematician <a href="/wiki/Cahit_Arf" title="Cahit Arf">Cahit Arf</a>, who defined the <a href="/wiki/Arf_invariant" title="Arf invariant">Arf invariant</a>; and immunologists <a href="/wiki/U%C4%9Fur_%C5%9Eahin" title="Uğur Şahin">Uğur Şahin</a> and <a href="/wiki/%C3%96zlem_T%C3%BCreci" title="Özlem Türeci">Özlem Türeci</a>, whose German <a href="/wiki/Biotechnology" title="Biotechnology">biotechnology</a> company, <a href="/wiki/BioNTech" title="BioNTech">BioNTech</a>, developed <a href="/wiki/RNA_vaccine" class="mw-redirect" title="RNA vaccine">one of the first efficacious vaccines</a> against <a href="/wiki/COVID-19" title="COVID-19">COVID-19</a>.
</p><p>Turkey is among the top fifty most innovative countries in the world, ranking 41st in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index" title="Global Innovation Index">Global Innovation Index</a> in 2021; this represents a considerable increase since 2011, where it was ranked 65th.<sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Demographics">Demographics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Turkey" title="Demographics of Turkey">Demographics of Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Turkish_people" title="Turkish people">Turkish people</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg/220px-Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="124" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg/330px-Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg/440px-Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3633" data-file-height="2044" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Istanbul_Levent_skyline.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a> is the most populous city in Turkey and the country's largest economic and financial centre.<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>According to the <i>Address-Based Population Recording System</i> of Turkey, the country's population was 84,680,273 in 2021,<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> 93.2% of whom lived in <a href="/wiki/Urban_area" title="Urban area">province and district centers</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> while only 6.8% lived in towns and villages.<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> According to the 2021 estimate, the population increased by 1.27 percent compared to the previous year.<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, Turkey had an average population density of 110 people per km².<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> People within the 15–64 <a href="/wiki/Age_group" class="mw-redirect" title="Age group">age group</a> constituted 67.9 percent of the total population; the 0–14 age group corresponded to 22.4 percent; while senior citizens aged 65 years or older made up 9.7 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-2021stat_403-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2021stat-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Article 66 of the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Constitution" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish Constitution">Turkish Constitution</a> defines a "Turk" as "anyone who is bound to the Turkish state through the bond of citizenship"; therefore, the legal use of the term "Turkish" as a <a href="/wiki/Citizenship" title="Citizenship">citizen</a> of Turkey is different from the <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_group" title="Ethnic group">ethnic</a> definition.<sup id="cite_ref-:02_404-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-404">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup> However approximately 70 to 80 percent of the country's citizens are ethnic Turks.<sup id="cite_ref-konda2_405-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-konda2-405">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cia_4-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-4">&#91;4&#93;</a></sup> It is estimated that there are at least 47 ethnic groups represented in Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-mutlu_406-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mutlu-406">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup> Reliable data on the ethnic mix of the population is not available, because Turkish census figures do not include statistics on ethnicity.<sup id="cite_ref-Turkey_Ethnic_groups_407-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Turkey_Ethnic_groups-407">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png/220px-Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="94" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png/330px-Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png/440px-Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png 2x" data-file-width="1579" data-file-height="677" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Turkey_total_fertility_rate_by_province_2021.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Total_fertility_rate" title="Total fertility rate">Total fertility rate</a> in <a href="/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependencies_by_total_fertility_rate" title="List of sovereign states and dependencies by total fertility rate">Turkey</a> by <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_Turkey" title="Provinces of Turkey">province</a> (2021)<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup> <style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#ffff00; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;3–4</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"/><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#0cff00; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;2–3</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"/><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#24e0d9; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;1.5-2</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"/><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#3aafe0; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;1-1.5</div></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Kurds_in_Turkey" title="Kurds in Turkey">Kurds</a> are the largest non-Turkish ethnicity at anywhere from 12–25 per cent of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-kirisci_410-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kirisci-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> The exact figure remains a subject of dispute; according to Servet Mutlu, "more often than not, these estimates reflect pro-Kurdish or pro-Turkish sympathies and attitudes rather than scientific facts or erudition".<sup id="cite_ref-mutlu_406-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mutlu-406">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup> Mutlu's 1990 study estimated Kurds made up around 12 per cent of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;411&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Kurds" title="Kurds">Kurds</a> make up a majority in the provinces of <a href="/wiki/A%C4%9Fr%C4%B1_Province" title="Ağrı Province">Ağrı</a>, <a href="/wiki/Batman_Province" title="Batman Province">Batman</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bing%C3%B6l_Province" title="Bingöl Province">Bingöl</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bitlis_Province" title="Bitlis Province">Bitlis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Diyarbak%C4%B1r_Province" title="Diyarbakır Province">Diyarbakır</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hakkari_Province" class="mw-redirect" title="Hakkari Province">Hakkari</a>, <a href="/wiki/I%C4%9Fd%C4%B1r_Province" title="Iğdır Province">Iğdır</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mardin_Province" title="Mardin Province">Mardin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mu%C5%9F_Province" title="Muş Province">Muş</a>, <a href="/wiki/Siirt_Province" title="Siirt Province">Siirt</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C5%9E%C4%B1rnak_Province" title="Şırnak Province">Şırnak</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tunceli_Province" title="Tunceli Province">Tunceli</a> and <a href="/wiki/Van_Province" title="Van Province">Van</a>; a near majority in <a href="/wiki/%C5%9Eanl%C4%B1urfa_Province" title="Şanlıurfa Province">Şanlıurfa Province</a> (47%); and a large minority in <a href="/wiki/Kars_Province" title="Kars Province">Kars Province</a> (20%).<sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup> In addition, due to internal migration, <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_diaspora" class="mw-redirect" title="Kurdish diaspora">Kurdish diaspora</a> communities exist in all of the major cities in central and western Turkey. In Istanbul, there are an estimated three million Kurds, making it the city with the largest Kurdish population in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-Nachmani2003_413-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Nachmani2003-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup> Non-Kurdish minorities are believed to make up an estimated 7–12 percent of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_4-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-4">&#91;4&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The three "<a href="/wiki/Millet_(Ottoman_Empire)" title="Millet (Ottoman Empire)">Non-Muslim</a>" minority groups recognised in the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Lausanne" title="Treaty of Lausanne">Treaty of Lausanne</a> were <a href="/wiki/Armenians_in_Turkey" title="Armenians in Turkey">Armenians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Greeks_in_Turkey" title="Greeks in Turkey">Greeks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jews_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Jews in Turkey">Jews</a>. Other ethnic groups include <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_Turkey" title="Albanians in Turkey">Albanians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arabs_in_Turkey" title="Arabs in Turkey">Arabs</a>, <a href="/wiki/Assyrians_in_Turkey" title="Assyrians in Turkey">Assyrians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bosniaks_in_Turkey" title="Bosniaks in Turkey">Bosniaks</a>, <a href="/wiki/Circassians_in_Turkey" title="Circassians in Turkey">Circassians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Georgians_in_Turkey" title="Georgians in Turkey">Georgians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Laz_people" title="Laz people">Laz</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pomaks" title="Pomaks">Pomaks</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Romani_people" title="Romani people">Roma</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_4-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-4">&#91;4&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Roopnarine2015_414-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roopnarine2015-414">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-MedinaHepner2013_415-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MedinaHepner2013-415">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup> Turkey is also home to a Muslim community of <a href="/wiki/Megleno-Romanians" title="Megleno-Romanians">Megleno-Romanians</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-megl_418-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-megl-418">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Before the start of the <a href="/wiki/Syrian_civil_war" title="Syrian civil war">Syrian civil war</a> in 2011, the estimated number of <a href="/wiki/Arabs_in_Turkey" title="Arabs in Turkey">Arabs in Turkey</a> varied from 1 million to more than 2 million.<sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup> As of April 2020, there are 3.6 million <a href="/wiki/Refugees_of_the_Syrian_Civil_War_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Refugees of the Syrian Civil War in Turkey">Syrian refugees</a> in Turkey, who are mostly Arabs but also include <a href="/wiki/Syrian_Kurds" class="mw-redirect" title="Syrian Kurds">Syrian Kurds</a>, <a href="/wiki/Syrian_Turkmen" title="Syrian Turkmen">Syrian Turkmen</a>, and other <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_groups_of_Syria" class="mw-redirect" title="Ethnic groups of Syria">ethnic groups of Syria</a>. The vast majority of these are living in Turkey with temporary residence permits. The Turkish government has granted Turkish citizenship to refugees who have joined the <a href="/wiki/Syrian_National_Army" title="Syrian National Army">Syrian National Army</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-unhcr-syrian-refugees_420-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unhcr-syrian-refugees-420">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-422" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-422">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
