<p>The Byzantine era is usually dated from 330 AD, when <a href="/wiki/Constantine_the_Great" title="Constantine the Great">Constantine the Great</a> moved the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman</a> capital to <a href="/wiki/Byzantium" title="Byzantium">Byzantium</a>, which became <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a>, until the fall of the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine Empire</a> in 1453. Its architecture dramatically influenced the later medieval architecture throughout Europe and the Near East, and became the primary progenitor of the Renaissance and Ottoman architectural traditions that followed its collapse.<sup id="cite_ref-518" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-518">&#91;518&#93;</a></sup> When the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman Empire</a> went Christian (as well as eastwards) with Constantinople as its new capital, its architecture became more sensuous and more ambitious. This new style, which would come to be known as <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_architecture" title="Byzantine architecture">Byzantine architecture</a>, with increasingly exotic domes and ever-richer mosaics, spread west to <a href="/wiki/Ravenna" title="Ravenna">Ravenna</a> and <a href="/wiki/Venice" title="Venice">Venice</a> in Italy, and as far north as <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a> in Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-519" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-519">&#91;519&#93;</a></sup> This influence can be seen particularly in the <a href="/wiki/Venetian_Gothic_architecture" title="Venetian Gothic architecture">Venetian Gothic architecture</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Seljuk_architecture" title="Seljuk architecture">architecture of the Seljuk Turks</a> combined the elements and characteristics of the <a href="/wiki/Architecture_of_Central_Asia" title="Architecture of Central Asia">Turkic architecture of Central Asia</a> with those of <a href="/wiki/Persian_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Persian architecture">Persian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arab_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Arab architecture">Arab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Armenian_architecture" title="Armenian architecture">Armenian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_architecture" title="Byzantine architecture">Byzantine</a> architecture. The transition from Seljuk architecture to <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_architecture" title="Ottoman architecture">Ottoman architecture</a> is most visible in <a href="/wiki/Bursa" title="Bursa">Bursa</a>, which was the capital of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman State</a> between 1335 and 1413. Following the <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople" title="Fall of Constantinople">Ottoman conquest of Constantinople (Istanbul)</a> in 1453, Ottoman architecture was significantly influenced by <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_architecture" title="Byzantine architecture">Byzantine architecture</a>. <a href="/wiki/Topkap%C4%B1_Palace" title="Topkapı Palace">Topkapı Palace</a> in Istanbul is one of the most famous examples of <a href="/wiki/Classical_Ottoman_architecture" title="Classical Ottoman architecture">classical Ottoman architecture</a> and was the primary residence of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Sultan" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman Sultan">Ottoman Sultans</a> for approximately 400 years.<sup id="cite_ref-autogenerated2_520-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autogenerated2-520">&#91;520&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Mimar_Sinan" title="Mimar Sinan">Mimar Sinan</a> (c.1489–1588) was the most important architect of the classical period in Ottoman architecture. He was the chief architect of at least 374 buildings that were constructed in various <a href="/wiki/Eyalet" title="Eyalet">provinces</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> in the 16th century.<sup id="cite_ref-521" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-521">&#91;521&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Sedefkar_Mehmed_Agha" title="Sedefkar Mehmed Agha">Sedefkar Mehmed Ağa</a>, the architect of the <a href="/wiki/Blue_Mosque,_Istanbul" title="Blue Mosque, Istanbul">Blue Mosque</a> in Istanbul, was an apprentice of Mimar Sinan, later becoming his first assistant in charge of the office of chief architect during his absence. Mimar Sinan's works had a significant influence on Sedefkar Mehmed Ağa.
</p><p>Since the 18th century, Turkish architecture has been increasingly influenced by European styles, and this can be particularly seen in the <a href="/wiki/Tanzimat" title="Tanzimat">Tanzimat</a> era buildings of Istanbul like the <a href="/wiki/Dolmabah%C3%A7e_Palace" title="Dolmabahçe Palace">Dolmabahçe</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C3%87%C4%B1ra%C4%9Fan_Palace" title="Çırağan Palace">Çırağan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Taksim_Military_Barracks" title="Taksim Military Barracks">Taksim Military Barracks</a> (demolished), <a href="/wiki/Feriye_Saraylar%C4%B1" class="mw-redirect" title="Feriye Sarayları">Feriye</a>, <a href="/wiki/Beylerbeyi_Palace" title="Beylerbeyi Palace">Beylerbeyi</a>, <a href="/wiki/K%C3%BC%C3%A7%C3%BCksu_Palace" class="mw-redirect" title="Küçüksu Palace">Küçüksu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ihlamur_Palace" class="mw-redirect" title="Ihlamur Palace">Ihlamur</a> and <a href="/wiki/Y%C4%B1ld%C4%B1z_Palace" title="Yıldız Palace">Yıldız</a> <a href="/wiki/Palace" title="Palace">palaces</a>, which were all designed by members of the <a href="/wiki/Balyan_family" title="Balyan family">Balyan family</a> of Ottoman Armenian court architects.<sup id="cite_ref-522" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-522">&#91;522&#93;</a></sup> The Ottoman era <a href="/wiki/Yal%C4%B1" title="Yalı">waterfront houses (<i>yalı</i>)</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Bosphorus" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosphorus">Bosphorus</a> also reflect the fusion between classical Ottoman and European architectural styles during the aforementioned period. Italian architect, <a href="/wiki/Raimondo_D%27Aronco" title="Raimondo D&#39;Aronco">Raimondo D'Aronco</a> served as the chief palace architect to the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II in Istanbul for 16 years. D'Aronco designed and built a large number of buildings of various types in Istanbul. The stylistic features of his works can be classified in three groups: Revivalism, reinterpretation of the Ottoman forms, Art Nouveau and Vienna Secession. Art Nouveau was first introduced to Istanbul by D'Aronco, and his designs reveal that he drew freely on Byzantine and Ottoman decorations. He also mixed Western and Oriental styles in his work.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/First_National_Architectural_Movement" class="mw-redirect" title="First National Architectural Movement">First National Architectural Movement</a> in the early 20th century sought to create a new architecture, which was based on motifs from Seljuk and Ottoman architecture. The leading architects of this movement were <a href="/wiki/Vedat_Tek" title="Vedat Tek">Vedat Tek</a> (1873–1942), <a href="/wiki/Mimar_Kemaleddin_Bey" class="mw-redirect" title="Mimar Kemaleddin Bey">Mimar Kemaleddin Bey</a> (1870–1927), <a href="/wiki/Arif_Hikmet_Koyuno%C4%9Flu" title="Arif Hikmet Koyunoğlu">Arif Hikmet Koyunoğlu</a> (1888–1982) and Giulio Mongeri (1873–1953).<sup id="cite_ref-turkisharch_523-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-turkisharch-523">&#91;523&#93;</a></sup> Buildings from this era are the <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Main_Post_Office" class="mw-redirect" title="Istanbul Main Post Office">Grand Post Office</a> in Istanbul (1905–1909), <a href="/wiki/Tayyare_Apartments" title="Tayyare Apartments">Tayyare Apartments</a> (1919–1922),<sup id="cite_ref-tayyare_524-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tayyare-524">&#91;524&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_4th_Vak%C4%B1f_Han" title="Istanbul 4th Vakıf Han">Istanbul 4th Vakıf Han</a> (1911–1926),<sup id="cite_ref-525" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-525">&#91;525&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/State_Art_and_Sculpture_Museum" title="State Art and Sculpture Museum">State Art and Sculpture Museum</a> (1927–1930),<sup id="cite_ref-stateart_526-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-stateart-526">&#91;526&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ethnography_Museum_of_Ankara" title="Ethnography Museum of Ankara">Ethnography Museum of Ankara</a> (1925–1928),<sup id="cite_ref-Ethnography_527-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ethnography-527">&#91;527&#93;</a></sup> the first <a href="/wiki/Ziraat_Bank" title="Ziraat Bank">Ziraat Bank</a> headquarters in Ankara (1925–1929),<sup id="cite_ref-528" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-528">&#91;528&#93;</a></sup> the first <a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrkiye_%C4%B0%C5%9F_Bankas%C4%B1" class="mw-redirect" title="Türkiye İş Bankası">Türkiye İş Bankası</a> headquarters in Ankara (1926–1929),<sup id="cite_ref-işbank_529-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-işbank-529">&#91;529&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Bebek,_Istanbul" class="mw-redirect" title="Bebek, Istanbul">Bebek</a> <a href="/wiki/Bebek_Mosque" title="Bebek Mosque">Mosque</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-bebek_530-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bebek-530">&#91;530&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Turkish_cuisine" title="Turkish cuisine">Turkish cuisine</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_cuisine" title="Ottoman cuisine">Ottoman cuisine</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:204px;max-width:204px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg/200px-Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="137" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg/300px-Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg/400px-Turkish_coffee_in_Istanbul.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2510" data-file-height="1719" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Turkish_coffee" title="Turkish coffee">Turkish coffee</a> with <a href="/wiki/Turkish_delight" title="Turkish delight">Turkish delight</a>. Turkish coffee is a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists" title="UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists">UNESCO-listed intangible cultural heritage</a> of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_people" title="Turkish people">Turks</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-531" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-531">&#91;531&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-532" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-532">&#91;532&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG/200px-Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG" decoding="async" width="200" height="117" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG/300px-Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG/400px-Meze_Lido_Restaurant_Adalar.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4841" data-file-height="2844" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Turkish_cuisine" title="Turkish cuisine">Turkish cuisine</a> is largely the heritage of <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_cuisine" title="Ottoman cuisine">Ottoman cuisine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-İlkin-Kaufman_533-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-İlkin-Kaufman-533">&#91;533&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Aarssen-Backus_534-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aarssen-Backus-534">&#91;534&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Turkish_cuisine" title="Turkish cuisine">Turkish cuisine</a> is largely the heritage of <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_cuisine" title="Ottoman cuisine">Ottoman cuisine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-İlkin-Kaufman_533-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-İlkin-Kaufman-533">&#91;533&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Aarssen-Backus_534-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aarssen-Backus-534">&#91;534&#93;</a></sup> In the early years of the Republic, a few studies were published about regional Anatolian dishes but cuisine did not feature heavily in Turkish folkloric studies until the 1980s, when the fledgling tourism industry encouraged the Turkish state to sponsor two food symposia. The papers submitted at the symposia presented the history of Turkish cuisine on a "historical continuum" that dated back to Turkic origins in Central Asia and continued through the Seljuk and Ottoman periods.<sup id="cite_ref-berg_535-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-berg-535">&#91;535&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Many of the papers presented at these first two symposia were unreferenced. Prior to the symposia, the study of Turkish culinary culture was first popularised by the publication of Süheyl Ünver's <i>Fifty Dishes in Turkish History</i> in 1948. This book was based on recipes found in an 18th century Ottoman manuscript. His second book was about the 15th century palace cuisine during the reign of Sultan <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_II" title="Mehmed II">Mehmed II</a>. Following the publication of Ünver's book, subsequent studies were published, including a 1978 study by a historian named Bahaettin Ögel about the <a href="/wiki/Central_Asian_cuisine" title="Central Asian cuisine">Central Asian</a> origins of Turkish cuisine.<sup id="cite_ref-berg_535-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-berg-535">&#91;535&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Ottoman_cuisine" title="Ottoman cuisine">Ottoman cuisine</a> contains elements of <a href="/wiki/Turkish_cuisine" title="Turkish cuisine">Turkish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_cuisine" title="Byzantine cuisine">Byzantine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Balkan_cuisine" title="Balkan cuisine">Balkan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Armenian_cuisine" title="Armenian cuisine">Armenian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Georgian_cuisine" title="Georgian cuisine">Georgian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_cuisine" title="Kurdish cuisine">Kurdish</a>,  <a href="/wiki/Arab_cuisine" title="Arab cuisine">Arab</a> and <a href="/wiki/Persian_cuisine" class="mw-redirect" title="Persian cuisine">Persian</a> cuisines.<sup id="cite_ref-İlkin-Kaufman_533-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-İlkin-Kaufman-533">&#91;533&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Aarssen-Backus_534-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aarssen-Backus-534">&#91;534&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-536" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-536">&#91;536&#93;</a></sup> It can be described as a fusion and refinement of <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_cuisine" title="Mediterranean cuisine">Mediterranean</a>, <a href="/wiki/Middle_Eastern_cuisine" title="Middle Eastern cuisine">Middle Eastern</a>, <a href="/wiki/Central_Asian_cuisine" title="Central Asian cuisine">Central Asian</a>, Balkan and <a href="/wiki/Eastern_European_cuisine" title="Eastern European cuisine">Eastern European</a> cuisines.<sup id="cite_ref-İlkin-Kaufman_533-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-İlkin-Kaufman-533">&#91;533&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Aarssen-Backus_534-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aarssen-Backus-534">&#91;534&#93;</a></sup> The country's position between Europe, Asia and the Mediterranean Sea helped the Turks in gaining complete control of the major <a href="/wiki/Trade_route" title="Trade route">trade routes</a>, and an ideal landscape and climate allowed plants and animals to flourish. Turkish cuisine was well established by the mid-1400s, which marked the beginning of the <a href="/wiki/Classical_Age_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Classical Age of the Ottoman Empire">classical age</a> during the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>'s 623-year history. <a href="/wiki/Yogurt" title="Yogurt">Yogurt</a> salads; <a href="/wiki/Meze" title="Meze">mezes</a>; fish and seafood; grilled, sauteed or steamed meat varieties; vegetables or <a href="/wiki/Dolma" title="Dolma">stuffed and wrapped vegetables</a> cooked with <a href="/wiki/Olive_oil" title="Olive oil">olive oil</a>; and drinks like <a href="/wiki/Sharbat_(beverage)" title="Sharbat (beverage)">sherbet</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ayran" title="Ayran">ayran</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rak%C4%B1" title="Rakı">rakı</a> became Turkish staples. The empire, eventually spanning from Austria and Ukraine in the north to Yemen and Sudan in the south, Algeria and the Maghreb in the west to the Caspian Sea and Persian Gulf in the east, used its land and water routes to import exotic ingredients from all over the world. By the end of the 16th century, the Ottoman court housed over 1,400 live-in cooks and passed laws regulating the freshness of food. Since the fall of the empire in World War I (1914–1918) and the establishment of the Turkish Republic in 1923, foreign food such as French hollandaise sauce and Western fast food have made their way into the modern Turkish diet.<sup id="cite_ref-foodbycountry.com_537-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-foodbycountry.com-537">&#91;537&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sports">Sports</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sports_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Sports in Turkey">Sports in Turkey</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Football_in_Turkey" title="Football in Turkey">Football in Turkey</a></div>
<p>The most popular <a href="/wiki/Sports_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Sports in Turkey">sport in Turkey</a> is <a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">association football</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-538" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-538">&#91;538&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Galatasaray_S.K._(football)" title="Galatasaray S.K. (football)">Galatasaray</a> won the <a href="/wiki/2000_UEFA_Cup_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="2000 UEFA Cup Final">UEFA Cup</a> and <a href="/wiki/2000_UEFA_Super_Cup" title="2000 UEFA Super Cup">UEFA Super Cup</a> in 2000.<sup id="cite_ref-uefa.com_539-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-uefa.com-539">&#91;539&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Turkish_national_football_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkish national football team">Turkish national football team</a> won the bronze medal at the <a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">2002 FIFA World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/2003_FIFA_Confederations_Cup" title="2003 FIFA Confederations Cup">2003 FIFA Confederations Cup</a> and <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008" title="UEFA Euro 2008">UEFA Euro 2008</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-tff.org1_540-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tff.org1-540">&#91;540&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg/220px-La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg/330px-La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg/440px-La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:La_selecci%C3%B3n_turca_de_baloncesto_tras_recibir_la_medalla_de_plata.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Turkey_national_basketball_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkey national basketball team">Turkey</a> won numerous international accolades, including the silver medal at the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIBA_World_Championship" title="2010 FIBA World Championship">2010 FIBA World Championship</a>.</div></div></div>
<p>Other mainstream sports such as <a href="/wiki/Basketball" title="Basketball">basketball</a> and <a href="/wiki/Volleyball" title="Volleyball">volleyball</a> are also popular.<sup id="cite_ref-541" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-541">&#91;541&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Turkey_national_basketball_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Turkey national basketball team">men's national basketball team</a> won the silver medal at the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIBA_World_Championship" title="2010 FIBA World Championship">2010 FIBA World Championship</a> and at <a href="/wiki/EuroBasket_2001" title="EuroBasket 2001">EuroBasket 2001</a>, which were both hosted by Turkey; and is one of the most successful at the <a href="/wiki/Basketball_at_the_Mediterranean_Games" title="Basketball at the Mediterranean Games">Mediterranean Games</a>. <a href="/wiki/Anadolu_Efes_S.K." title="Anadolu Efes S.K.">Anadolu Efes S.K.</a>, the most successful Turkish basketball club in international competitions, won the <a href="/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_EuroLeague" title="2021–22 EuroLeague">2021–22 EuroLeague</a>, <a href="/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_EuroLeague" title="2020–21 EuroLeague">2020–21 EuroLeague</a> and the <a href="/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_FIBA_Kora%C4%87_Cup" title="1995–96 FIBA Korać Cup">1995–96</a> <a href="/wiki/FIBA_Kora%C4%87_Cup" title="FIBA Korać Cup">FIBA Korać Cup</a>; were the runners-up of the <a href="/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EuroLeague" title="2018–19 EuroLeague">2018–19 EuroLeague</a> and the <a href="/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_FIBA_European_Cup" title="1992–93 FIBA European Cup">1992–93</a> <a href="/wiki/FIBA_Saporta_Cup" title="FIBA Saporta Cup">FIBA Saporta Cup</a>; and finished third at the <a href="/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_FIBA_EuroLeague" title="1999–2000 FIBA EuroLeague">1999–2000 EuroLeague</a> and the <a href="/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_FIBA_SuproLeague" title="2000–01 FIBA SuproLeague">2000–01 SuproLeague</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-542" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-542">&#91;542&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-543" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-543">&#91;543&#93;</a></sup> When the <a href="/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_EuroLeague_Regular_Season" title="2019–20 EuroLeague Regular Season">2019–20 EuroLeague Regular Season</a> was suspended on 12 March 2020 due to the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Europe" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Europe">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, Anadolu Efes S.K. <a href="/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_EuroLeague#League_table" title="2019–20 EuroLeague">ranked 1st in the league table</a>. Another successful Turkish basketball club, <a href="/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_Men%27s_Basketball" class="mw-redirect" title="Fenerbahçe Men&#39;s Basketball">Fenerbahçe</a> reached the Final of the <a href="/wiki/EuroLeague" title="EuroLeague">EuroLeague</a> in three consecutive seasons (<a href="/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Euroleague" title="2015–16 Euroleague">2016</a>, <a href="/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_EuroLeague" title="2016–17 EuroLeague">2017</a> and <a href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EuroLeague" title="2017–18 EuroLeague">2018</a>), becoming the European champions in 2017 and runners-up in 2016 and 2018. <a href="/wiki/Galatasaray_S.K._(men%27s_basketball)" title="Galatasaray S.K. (men&#39;s basketball)">Galatasaray</a> won the <a href="/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Eurocup_Basketball" title="2015–16 Eurocup Basketball">2015–16 Eurocup</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Be%C5%9Fikta%C5%9F_men%27s_basketball_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Beşiktaş men&#39;s basketball team">Beşiktaş</a> won the <a href="/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_FIBA_EuroChallenge" title="2011–12 FIBA EuroChallenge">2011–12 FIBA EuroChallenge</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-fibaeurope.com1_544-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fibaeurope.com1-544">&#91;544&#93;</a></sup> The Final of the <a href="/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_EuroLeague_Women" title="2013–14 EuroLeague Women">2013–14 EuroLeague Women</a> basketball championship was played between two Turkish teams, <a href="/wiki/Galatasaray_S.K._(women%27s_basketball)" title="Galatasaray S.K. (women&#39;s basketball)">Galatasaray</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_Women%27s_Basketball" class="mw-redirect" title="Fenerbahçe Women&#39;s Basketball">Fenerbahçe</a>, and won by Galatasaray.<sup id="cite_ref-fibaeurope.com2_545-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fibaeurope.com2-545">&#91;545&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Turkey_women%27s_national_basketball_team" title="Turkey women&#39;s national basketball team">women's national basketball team</a> won the silver medal at the <a href="/wiki/EuroBasket_Women_2011" title="EuroBasket Women 2011">EuroBasket Women 2011</a> and the bronze medal at the <a href="/wiki/EuroBasket_Women_2013" title="EuroBasket Women 2013">EuroBasket Women 2013</a>. Like the men's team, the women's basketball team is one of the most successful at the <a href="/wiki/Basketball_at_the_Mediterranean_Games" title="Basketball at the Mediterranean Games">Mediterranean Games</a>.
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg/220px-Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg/440px-Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5472" data-file-height="3648" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Vakifbanksk2018cl.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Vak%C4%B1fBank_S.K." title="VakıfBank S.K.">VakıfBank S.K.</a> has won the <a href="/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">FIVB Volleyball Women's Club World Championship</a> in <a href="/wiki/2017_FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="2017 FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2017</a> and <a href="/wiki/2018_FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="2018 FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2018</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-fenerbahce.org.tr_546-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fenerbahce.org.tr-546">&#91;546&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-eczacibasisporkulubu.org.tr_547-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-eczacibasisporkulubu.org.tr-547">&#91;547&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-hurriyet.com.tr1_548-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hurriyet.com.tr1-548">&#91;548&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_CEV_Women%27s_Champions_League" title="2017–18 CEV Women&#39;s Champions League">2017–18 CEV Women's Champions League</a> for the fourth time in their history.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_549-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-549">&#91;549&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Turkey_women%27s_national_volleyball_team" title="Turkey women&#39;s national volleyball team">women's national volleyball team</a> won the gold medal at the <a href="/wiki/2015_European_Games" title="2015 European Games">2015 European Games</a>, the silver medal at the <a href="/wiki/2003_Women%27s_European_Volleyball_Championship" title="2003 Women&#39;s European Volleyball Championship">2003 European Championship</a>, the bronze medal at the <a href="/wiki/2011_Women%27s_European_Volleyball_Championship" title="2011 Women&#39;s European Volleyball Championship">2011 European Championship</a>, and the bronze medal at the <a href="/wiki/2012_FIVB_World_Grand_Prix" class="mw-redirect" title="2012 FIVB World Grand Prix">2012 FIVB World Grand Prix</a>. They also won multiple medals over multiple decades at the <a href="/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_Mediterranean_Games" title="Volleyball at the Mediterranean Games">Mediterranean Games</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-tvf.org.tr_550-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tvf.org.tr-550">&#91;550&#93;</a></sup> Women's volleyball clubs, namely <a href="/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_Women%27s_Volleyball" class="mw-redirect" title="Fenerbahçe Women&#39;s Volleyball">Fenerbahçe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eczac%C4%B1ba%C5%9F%C4%B1_Istanbul" class="mw-redirect" title="Eczacıbaşı Istanbul">Eczacıbaşı</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vak%C4%B1fbank_Spor_Kul%C3%BCb%C3%BC" class="mw-redirect" title="Vakıfbank Spor Kulübü">Vakıfbank</a>, have won numerous European championship titles and medals. <a href="/wiki/Fenerbah%C3%A7e_Women%27s_Volleyball" class="mw-redirect" title="Fenerbahçe Women&#39;s Volleyball">Fenerbahçe</a> won the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIVB_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" class="mw-redirect" title="2010 FIVB Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2010 FIVB Women's Club World Championship</a> and the <a href="/wiki/CEV_Women%27s_Champions_League" title="CEV Women&#39;s Champions League">2012 CEV Women's Champions League</a>. Representing <a href="/wiki/European_Volleyball_Confederation" title="European Volleyball Confederation">Europe</a> as the winner of the <a href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_CEV_Women%27s_Champions_League" title="2012–13 CEV Women&#39;s Champions League">2012–13 CEV Women's Champions League</a>, Vakıfbank also became the world champion by winning the <a href="/wiki/2013_FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="2013 FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2013 FIVB Volleyball Women's Club World Championship</a>. Recently Vakıfbank has won the <a href="/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">FIVB Volleyball Women's Club World Championship</a> in <a href="/wiki/2017_FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="2017 FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2017</a> and <a href="/wiki/2018_FIVB_Volleyball_Women%27s_Club_World_Championship" title="2018 FIVB Volleyball Women&#39;s Club World Championship">2018</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-fenerbahce.org.tr_546-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fenerbahce.org.tr-546">&#91;546&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-eczacibasisporkulubu.org.tr_547-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-eczacibasisporkulubu.org.tr-547">&#91;547&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-hurriyet.com.tr1_548-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hurriyet.com.tr1-548">&#91;548&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_CEV_Women%27s_Champions_League" title="2017–18 CEV Women&#39;s Champions League">2017–18 CEV Women's Champions League</a> for the fourth time in their history.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_549-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-549">&#91;549&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The traditional national sport of Turkey has been <a href="/wiki/Oil_wrestling" title="Oil wrestling">yağlı güreş</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Olive_oil" title="Olive oil">oil</a> <a href="/wiki/Wrestling" title="Wrestling">wrestling</a></i>) since Ottoman times.<sup id="cite_ref-551" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-551">&#91;551&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Edirne_Province" title="Edirne Province">Edirne Province</a> has hosted the annual <a href="/wiki/K%C4%B1rkp%C4%B1nar" title="Kırkpınar">Kırkpınar</a> oil wrestling tournament since 1361, making it the oldest continuously held sporting competition in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-552" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-552">&#91;552&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-553" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-553">&#91;553&#93;</a></sup> In the 19th and early 20th centuries, Ottoman Turkish oil wrestling champions such as <a href="/wiki/Yusuf_%C4%B0smail" title="Yusuf İsmail">Koca Yusuf</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nurullah_Hasan" title="Nurullah Hasan">Nurullah Hasan</a> and <a href="/wiki/K%C4%B1z%C4%B1lc%C4%B1kl%C4%B1_Mahmut" title="Kızılcıklı Mahmut">Kızılcıklı Mahmut</a> acquired international fame in Europe and North America by winning world heavyweight wrestling championship titles. International wrestling styles governed by <a href="/wiki/International_Federation_of_Associated_Wrestling_Styles" class="mw-redirect" title="International Federation of Associated Wrestling Styles">FILA</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Freestyle_wrestling" title="Freestyle wrestling">freestyle wrestling</a> and <a href="/wiki/Greco-Roman_wrestling" title="Greco-Roman wrestling">Greco-Roman wrestling</a> are also popular, with many European, World and Olympic championship titles won by Turkish wrestlers both individually and as a national team.<sup id="cite_ref-554" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-554">&#91;554&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Media_and_cinema">Media and cinema</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Media_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Media in Turkey">Media in Turkey</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Turkey" title="Cinema of Turkey">Cinema of Turkey</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:282px;"><a href="/wiki/File:TRT_World.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/TRT_World.svg/280px-TRT_World.svg.png" decoding="async" width="280" height="37" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/TRT_World.svg/420px-TRT_World.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/TRT_World.svg/560px-TRT_World.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="930" data-file-height="123" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:TRT_World.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/TRT_World" title="TRT World">TRT World</a> is the international news platform of the <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Radio_and_Television_Corporation" title="Turkish Radio and Television Corporation">Turkish Radio and Television Corporation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-555" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-555">&#91;555&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Hundreds of television channels, thousands of local and national radio stations, several dozen newspapers, a productive and profitable <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Turkey" title="Cinema of Turkey">national cinema</a> and a rapid growth of <a href="/wiki/Broadband" title="Broadband">broadband</a> Internet use constitute a vibrant media industry in Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-tesevmedya_556-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tesevmedya-556">&#91;556&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-557" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-557">&#91;557&#93;</a></sup> The majority of the TV audiences are shared among public broadcaster <a href="/wiki/Turkish_Radio_and_Television_Corporation" title="Turkish Radio and Television Corporation">TRT</a> and the network-style channels such as <a href="/wiki/Kanal_D" title="Kanal D">Kanal D</a>, <a href="/wiki/Show_TV" title="Show TV">Show TV</a>, <a href="/wiki/ATV_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="ATV (Turkey)">ATV</a> and <a href="/wiki/Star_TV_(Turkey)" class="mw-redirect" title="Star TV (Turkey)">Star TV</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Broadcast_media" class="mw-redirect" title="Broadcast media">broadcast media</a> have a very high penetration as <a href="/wiki/Satellite_dishes" class="mw-redirect" title="Satellite dishes">satellite dishes</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cable_television" title="Cable television">cable</a> systems are widely available.<sup id="cite_ref-cp_558-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cp-558">&#91;558&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/RT%C3%9CK" class="mw-redirect" title="RTÜK">Radio and Television Supreme Council (RTÜK)</a> is the government body overseeing the broadcast media.<sup id="cite_ref-cp_558-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cp-558">&#91;558&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-559" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-559">&#91;559&#93;</a></sup> By circulation, the <a href="/wiki/List_of_newspapers_in_Turkey" title="List of newspapers in Turkey">most popular newspapers</a> are <i><a href="/wiki/Posta_(newspaper)" title="Posta (newspaper)">Posta</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/H%C3%BCrriyet" title="Hürriyet">Hürriyet</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/S%C3%B6zc%C3%BC" title="Sözcü">Sözcü</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Sabah_(newspaper)" title="Sabah (newspaper)">Sabah</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Habert%C3%BCrk" title="Habertürk">Habertürk</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-560" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-560">&#91;560&#93;</a></sup> 
<a href="/wiki/TRT_2" title="TRT 2">TRT 2</a> is the public service channel dedicated to culture and art.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Turkish_television_drama" title="Turkish television drama">Turkish television dramas</a> are increasingly becoming popular beyond Turkey's borders and are among the country's most vital exports, both in terms of profit and public relations.<sup id="cite_ref-561" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-561">&#91;561&#93;</a></sup> After sweeping the <a href="/wiki/Middle_East" title="Middle East">Middle East</a>'s television market over the past decade, Turkish shows have aired in more than a dozen <a href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South</a> and <a href="/wiki/Central_America" title="Central America">Central American</a> countries in 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-562" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-562">&#91;562&#93;</a></sup> Turkey is today the world's second largest exporter of television series.<sup id="cite_ref-563" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-563">&#91;563&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-564" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-564">&#91;564&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg/220px-Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg/330px-Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg/440px-Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4256" data-file-height="2832" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Aspendos_Amphitheatre.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The closing ceremony of the annual <a href="/wiki/International_Antalya_Golden_Orange_Film_Festival" class="mw-redirect" title="International Antalya Golden Orange Film Festival">International Antalya Golden Orange Film Festival</a> takes place at the virtually intact Roman theater in <a href="/wiki/Aspendos" title="Aspendos">Aspendos</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-565" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-565">&#91;565&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p><i><a href="/wiki/Ye%C5%9Fil%C3%A7am" class="mw-redirect" title="Yeşilçam">Yeşilçam</a></i> is the <a href="/wiki/Sobriquet" title="Sobriquet">sobriquet</a> that refers to the Turkish film art and industry. The first movie exhibited in the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> was the <a href="/wiki/Lumiere_Brothers" class="mw-redirect" title="Lumiere Brothers">Lumiere Brothers</a>' 1895 film, <i><a href="/wiki/L%27Arriv%C3%A9e_d%27un_train_en_gare_de_La_Ciotat" title="L&#39;Arrivée d&#39;un train en gare de La Ciotat">L'Arrivée d'un train en gare de La Ciotat</a></i>, which was shown in <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a> in 1896. The first Turkish-made film was a documentary entitled <i><a href="/wiki/Ayastefanos%27taki_Rus_Abidesinin_Y%C4%B1k%C4%B1l%C4%B1%C5%9F%C4%B1" title="Ayastefanos&#39;taki Rus Abidesinin Yıkılışı">Ayastefanos'taki Rus Abidesinin Yıkılışı</a></i> (<i>Demolition of the Russian Monument at <a href="/wiki/Ye%C5%9Filk%C3%B6y" title="Yeşilköy">San Stefano</a></i>), directed by <a href="/wiki/Fuat_Uzk%C4%B1nay" title="Fuat Uzkınay">Fuat Uzkınay</a> and completed in 1914. The first narrative film, <a href="/wiki/Sedat_Simavi" title="Sedat Simavi">Sedat Simavi</a>'s <i>The Spy</i>, was released in 1917. Turkey's first sound film was shown in 1931. Turkish directors like <a href="/wiki/Metin_Erksan" title="Metin Erksan">Metin Erksan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nuri_Bilge_Ceylan" title="Nuri Bilge Ceylan">Nuri Bilge Ceylan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Y%C4%B1lmaz_G%C3%BCney" title="Yılmaz Güney">Yılmaz Güney</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zeki_Demirkubuz" title="Zeki Demirkubuz">Zeki Demirkubuz</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ferzan_%C3%96zpetek" title="Ferzan Özpetek">Ferzan Özpetek</a> won numerous international awards such as the <a href="/wiki/Palme_d%27Or" title="Palme d&#39;Or">Palme d'Or</a> and <a href="/wiki/Golden_Bear" title="Golden Bear">Golden Bear</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-turkishculture.org5_566-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-turkishculture.org5-566">&#91;566&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-berlinale_1964_567-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-berlinale_1964-567">&#91;567&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Despite legal provisions, <a href="/wiki/Media_freedom_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Media freedom in Turkey">media freedom in Turkey</a> has steadily deteriorated from 2010 onwards, with a precipitous decline following the failed <a href="/wiki/2016_Turkish_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat_attempt" title="2016 Turkish coup d&#39;état attempt">coup attempt</a> on 15 July 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-568" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-568">&#91;568&#93;</a></sup> As of December 2016, at least 81 <a href="/wiki/List_of_arrested_journalists_in_Turkey" title="List of arrested journalists in Turkey">journalists were imprisoned</a> in Turkey and more than 100 news outlets were closed.<sup id="cite_ref-cpj.org1_282-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cpj.org1-282">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a> lists Turkey's <a href="/wiki/Media_freedom_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="Media freedom in Turkey">media</a> as <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_Press_(report)" title="Freedom of the Press (report)"><i>not free</i></a>.<sup id="cite_ref-freedomhouse_569-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-freedomhouse-569">&#91;569&#93;</a></sup> The media crackdowns also extend to <a href="/wiki/Internet_censorship" title="Internet censorship">Internet censorship</a> with <a href="/wiki/2017_block_of_Wikipedia_in_Turkey" class="mw-redirect" title="2017 block of Wikipedia in Turkey">Wikipedia getting blocked</a> between 29 April 2017 and 15 January 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-570" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-570">&#91;570&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-571" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-571">&#91;571&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
